# Business rules

The MVP product requirements the screens save through. Their rules hold however a change arrives: a screen, a file, an email, or the assistant.

## Org and access

The Compass org tree, Companies, Departments, Role Grants, scopes, and Settings.

<a id="req-org-0001"></a>

### Hold the Compass org tree

`REQ-ORG-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Iris holds the Compass org as a tree of Sectors, Regions, Districts, and Units, with Departments inside Units. Access, Settings, Agency approvals, and spend are all scoped by a node of this tree.
- **Why:** Spend must roll up the Compass structure *(PLT-2: Org hierarchy: sector → region → district → unit → department, with cost centers)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-2; [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) Departments within venues

**Rules**

- **R1.** A SECTOR node has no parent, a REGION sits under one SECTOR, a DISTRICT under one REGION, and a UNIT node under one DISTRICT; the tree has no other levels (C-9).
- **R2.** A node is saved only when its parent exists and is exactly one level above it; otherwise it is refused and the user is told why.
- **R3.** Two nodes under the same parent never share a name, two Sectors never share a name, and two Units never share a name anywhere in the program.
- **R4.** The ancestors of a node are its parent and each parent above that, up to its Sector.
- **R5.** A scope set at a node covers that node and every Unit beneath it.
- **R6.** Each UNIT node holds exactly one Unit, and the Unit's name is the node's name.
- **R7.** A Department belongs to one Unit and is the lowest level of the hierarchy; spend charged to it rolls up through its Unit, and no Role Grant, Setting, or Agency approval is scoped to it.

<a id="req-org-0002"></a>

### Add a Unit and its Departments

`REQ-ORG-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Program User, Unit User
- **What:** A Program User adds a Unit under a District by form, with its address, Company, Work Week start, and at least one Department. Iris sets the Unit's Market from its ZIP code.
- **Why:** Spend must roll up the Compass structure *(PLT-2: Org hierarchy: sector → region → district → unit → department, with cost centers)*
- **Sources:** [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Shift Creation; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-2; [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) Departments within venues

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User adds a Unit; it is saved as a UNIT node under an active District, together with one Unit record.
- **R2.** In MVP a Unit enters Iris only by this form or a UNITS file, never by sync from another system (C-8).
- **R3.** A Unit needs a name no other Unit has, address line, city, two-letter USPS state code, five-digit ZIP code, Company, and Work Week start day; one missing or malformed is refused.
- **R4.** The Unit's Market is the Market that holds its ZIP code; a ZIP code in no Market is refused.
- **R5.** The time zone is an IANA zone; when the form leaves it empty Iris fills it from the ZIP code, and refuses the Unit when it cannot place that ZIP code.
- **R6.** A Company name not yet on file is added as a new Company, and a name already on file is reused.
- **R7.** A Program User adds, renames, deactivates, or reactivates a Department; each has a name unique within its Unit and a cost center code no other Department has.
- **R8.** The Program User may mark the Unit a secured site and set its default parking, entrance, directions, site contact, and attire.
- **R9.** A Unit User whose Role Grant covers the Unit may change its default site instructions and no other Unit field.
- **R10.** A Program User may later change any Unit field, and changing the ZIP code sets the Market again by the same rule.
- **R11.** A Program User deactivates or reactivates a Unit by changing its node's active flag, reactivating only under an active District; an inactive Unit keeps its records and accepts no new Request.
- **R12.** When [`REQ-CATALOG-0002`](#req-catalog-0002) adds a ZIP code to a Market, every Unit with that ZIP code takes that Market; removing a ZIP code from a Market changes no Unit.
- **R13.** Changing a Unit's time zone moves no stored instant, so the local times and work dates of that Unit's Shifts and Timesheets are read in the new zone from then on.
- **R14.** A new Department copies its address and default site instructions from its Unit unless given, and a Program User may change them later.
- **R15.** Changing a Unit's address or default site instructions leaves each Department's copy as it was saved.
- **R16.** A Unit User whose Role Grant covers the Unit may change a Department's default parking, entrance, directions, site contact, and attire.
- **R17.** A Program User may name a Unit's primary operator, an active User with an unrevoked UNIT_USER grant covering the Unit, or leave it empty.
- **R18.** A primary operator who is deactivated or no longer covered by an unrevoked UNIT_USER grant is shown as none until a Program User names another.
- **R19.** A Unit is saved with at least one Department, and its last active Department cannot be deactivated while the Unit is active.

<a id="req-org-0003"></a>

### Load Units and Departments from a file

`REQ-ORG-0003`

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User loads many Units and their Departments at once from a UNITS file (C-8). The rows become a Proposal, and nothing is saved until the Program User approves it.
- **Why:** Spend must roll up the Compass structure *(PLT-2: Org hierarchy: sector → region → district → unit → department, with cost centers)*
- **Sources:** [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Shift Creation; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-2

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User sends a UNITS file, with one row for each Department of each Unit.
- **R2.** Each row must give sector, region, district, unit, address_line, city, state, zip, company, work_week_start, department, and department_cost_center.
- **R3.** The timezone, secured_site, and department address columns are optional; an empty timezone is filled from the ZIP code and an empty secured_site means not secured.
- **R4.** Each row is checked before the Proposal is shown, without saving, and again when it is saved, against [`REQ-ORG-0002.R1`](#req-org-0002), R3, R4, R5, and R7, so a ZIP code in no Market is a row problem.
- **R5.** A row that repeats an earlier row's Unit and Department is reported as a duplicate, and rows for one Unit that disagree on a Unit column are row problems.
- **R6.** A Sector, Region, or District that a row names but the tree lacks is a row problem whose proposed fix adds it through [`REQ-ORG-0008`](#req-org-0008) when accepted.
- **R7.** The rows of one file that name the same Unit share one group_key and are saved in one call, as that Unit and one Department for each row that names one.
- **R8.** A row whose unit is already a Unit in Iris is a row problem whose fix drops the row, because a UNITS file adds Units and never changes one.
- **R9.** A Department saved from a row copies the Unit's address where its address columns are empty, and its five site instructions, since the file has no instruction columns.

<a id="req-org-0005"></a>

### Grant a role within a scope

`REQ-ORG-0005` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin, Program User, Agency User
- **What:** A Role Grant gives one User one role and the scope it covers. Program Users, Agency Users, and Instawork Admins invite Users and grant or revoke roles within the limits below.
- **Why:**
  - Each persona gets its own view *(PLT-1: RBAC: unit (buyer), agency (supplier), corporate/program owner)*
  - MSP task: profile and password management *(PLT-4: User accounts with login, profiles and password management)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-1; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-4

**Rules**

- **R1.** A UNIT_USER grant names one org node at any level and no Agency, and covers every Unit at or beneath that node.
- **R2.** An AGENCY_USER grant names one Agency and no org node.
- **R3.** PROGRAM_USER and INSTAWORK_ADMIN grants name neither an org node nor an Agency, and a Program User covers the whole program.
- **R4.** A Program User may grant UNIT_USER, AGENCY_USER, and PROGRAM_USER to any User.
- **R5.** An Agency User may grant only AGENCY_USER, and only for the Agency of their own grant.
- **R6.** An Instawork Admin may grant only PROGRAM_USER, and only while no active User who has accepted their invite holds an unrevoked PROGRAM_USER grant.
- **R7.** At every start, when the User with the configured Instawork Admin email holds no INSTAWORK_ADMIN grant, Iris saves one with no granting User.
- **R8.** The grantee is an existing User, or a new one invited through [`REQ-IDENTITY-0002`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-identity-0002) in the same action; nobody is invited without a grant.
- **R9.** A User may hold several grants; one that repeats an unrevoked role and scope is refused, and granting a revoked one again clears its revoked_at and records the User who granted it again.
- **R10.** Whoever may grant a role and scope may revoke it; revoking sets revoked_at and ends that grant's access at once.
- **R11.** Through [`REQ-IDENTITY-0004`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-identity-0004), a Program User may deactivate or reactivate any User who is not an Instawork Admin, and an Agency User only one whose every grant is AGENCY_USER for their own Agency.
- **R12.** An invite, grant, revoke, or deactivation outside these limits is refused, nothing is saved, and the User is told why.
- **R13.** Whoever may grant a User's role and scope may send that User's invite again through [`REQ-IDENTITY-0002`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-identity-0002) until it is accepted.
- **R14.** A Program User sees every User and their Role Grants, and an Agency User sees only the Users who hold an AGENCY_USER grant for their own Agency.
- **R15.** An Instawork Admin may revoke a PROGRAM_USER grant, or send its invite again, only for a User who has not accepted their invite, and only while R6 would allow a grant.
- **R16.** An Instawork Admin sees only the Users whose PROGRAM_USER grant R15 or R18 lets them revoke, and the other Instawork Admins.
- **R17.** No User grants or revokes INSTAWORK_ADMIN.
- **R18.** An Instawork Admin may also revoke the PROGRAM_USER grant of the only active User who has accepted their invite and holds one, after which R6 allows a replacement.
- **R19.** Through [`REQ-IDENTITY-0004`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-identity-0004), an Instawork Admin may deactivate or reactivate another Instawork Admin, and never themselves.
- **R20.** AGENCY_USER is refused to a User holding an unrevoked INSTAWORK_ADMIN grant, and R7 seeds no INSTAWORK_ADMIN grant for a User holding an unrevoked AGENCY_USER grant.

<a id="req-org-0006"></a>

### Resolve a Setting for a Unit

`REQ-ORG-0006` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Given a Setting key and a Unit, Iris returns the value in force there. The nearest override up the org tree wins, then the program default, then the catalog default.
- **Why:**
  - Edits allowed for up to about 3 weeks make reporting stale *(TS-9: Configurable timesheet lock window (e.g. 24–48 hours after an event))*
  - Flag overtime rather than block it; some locations want a hard block, festivals accept overtime *(WA-19: Overtime tracking and alerts within each agency, with an optional hard block per location)*
  - Non-compliant spend persists through local relationships *(RC-11: Soft or hard gates for off-contract rates and non-contracted vendors)*
- **Sources:** [FAQ](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14WYK18DR1mu3SiXCUTRQw21Zjvzhl91U) Settings for each sector; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-9; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-19; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-11

**Rules**

- **R1.** For a key the catalog scopes as any, the value is the Setting row at the Unit's node, else the row at its nearest ancestor that has one.
- **R2.** When no node on that path has a row, the value is the program default row, which names no org node.
- **R3.** When there is no program default row, the value is the key's default in the settings catalog.
- **R4.** A key the catalog scopes as program needs no Unit and resolves only from the program default row, else the catalog default.
- **R5.** The value is returned in the key's catalog type: a whole number, true or false, or a gate mode of SOFT or HARD.

<a id="req-org-0008"></a>

### Add Sectors, Regions, and Districts by hand

`REQ-ORG-0008` · first slice

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User builds the upper levels of the org tree by hand. They add, rename, and deactivate Sectors, Regions, and Districts.
- **Why:** Spend must roll up the Compass structure *(PLT-2: Org hierarchy: sector → region → district → unit → department, with cost centers)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-2

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User adds a Sector, a Region under a Sector, or a District under a Region.
- **R2.** A new node needs a name and, below Sector level, an active parent one level up; it is saved active.
- **R3.** A name already used by another node under the same parent is refused, on add and on rename.
- **R4.** A Program User renames a node without changing its parent, its children, or anything scoped to it.
- **R5.** A Program User deactivates a Sector, Region, or District only when every node beneath it is inactive, and reactivates one only while its parent is active.

<a id="req-org-0009"></a>

### Allow each action only to its role and scope

`REQ-ORG-0009` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Before a person's action is saved or a record is shown, Iris checks the acting context of the request against the User's Role Grants. The action goes ahead only when the acting role allows it and an unrevoked grant for that role covers the record.
- **Why:** Each persona gets its own view *(PLT-1: RBAC: unit (buyer), agency (supplier), corporate/program owner)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-1; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §1 Who sees what

**Rules**

- **R1.** Each requirement names the roles that may take its action; a request whose acting role is not one of them is refused.
- **R2.** A Unit User acts only on Units at or beneath the org node of one of their UNIT_USER grants, and on records that belong to those Units.
- **R3.** An Agency User acts only on the records of the Agency in their acting context: Releases sent to it, its Workers, its Timesheets, its Rate Lines, and the records attached to these.
- **R4.** A Program User's scope is the whole program, so no Unit or Agency is outside it.
- **R5.** An Instawork Admin acts only on reference data (Positions, Markets, Market ZIP codes, labor rules), account teams, outside-system ids, Payment Terms, VMS fees, and what [`REQ-ORG-0005`](#req-org-0005) allows them.
- **R6.** A revoked Role Grant allows nothing, and no grant of an inactive User allows anything.
- **R7.** A list, search, or download returns only the records the acting context covers.
- **R8.** A refused action saves nothing, and the User is told that their role or scope does not allow it.
- **R9.** The acting context is one role and, for AGENCY_USER, one Agency; a UNIT_USER context covers the org nodes of all the User's unrevoked UNIT_USER grants.
- **R10.** A User sets or switches their acting context only to one that an unrevoked Role Grant of theirs gives, and it is kept on their session through [`REQ-IDENTITY-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-identity-0001).
- **R11.** Every request is checked against the acting context of its session, and is refused once the User holds no unrevoked grant for that role and Agency, whatever other grants they hold.
- **R12.** A session with no acting context yet may only list the contexts the User's unrevoked grants give, set one under R10, and sign out.
- **R13.** A request with no session, such as an inbound message, is checked against the acting context that the requirement handling it supplies.
- **R14.** A timed job acts as SYSTEM for no User, so this requirement does not check it.

<a id="req-org-0010"></a>

### Change a Setting

`REQ-ORG-0010`

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User changes the program default of a Setting, or overrides it for one Sector, Region, District, or Unit. The change applies the next time the Setting is resolved.
- **Why:**
  - Edits allowed for up to about 3 weeks make reporting stale *(TS-9: Configurable timesheet lock window (e.g. 24–48 hours after an event))*
  - Flag overtime rather than block it; some locations want a hard block, festivals accept overtime *(WA-19: Overtime tracking and alerts within each agency, with an optional hard block per location)*
- **Sources:** [FAQ](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14WYK18DR1mu3SiXCUTRQw21Zjvzhl91U) Settings for each sector; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-9; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-19

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User sets, changes, or removes a Setting value.
- **R2.** A key the catalog scopes as any takes a program default and an override at any Sector, Region, District, or Unit node, with one value per key and node.
- **R3.** A key the catalog scopes as program takes only a program default, and an override at an org node is refused.
- **R4.** A value that does not fit the key's catalog type (a whole number of 0 or more, true or false, or SOFT or HARD) is refused.
- **R5.** Removing an override deletes its row so the next value up the tree applies, and removing the program default restores the catalog default.

<a id="req-org-0011"></a>

### Assign Instawork's account team to parts of the org

`REQ-ORG-0011` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin, Program User, Unit User
- **What:** Instawork Admins name the Instawork Account Manager, Account Owner, and Support Lead for the whole program or any org node. Each Unit's team resolves from the nearest node above it, so Compass, Agencies, and Iris's agents know whom at Instawork to reach.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** Graph Instawork's Company admin keeps am_member and account reps through team_directory roles ACCOUNT_MANAGER and ACCOUNT_OWNER

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only an Instawork Admin assigns or removes an account team member.
- **R2.** An assignment names one AccountTeamRole, an active User holding an unrevoked INSTAWORK_ADMIN grant, and one org node, or no node for the whole program.
- **R3.** A scope has at most one open assignment per role, so a new assignment there first sets removed_at and removed_by_id on the open one.
- **R4.** Removing sets removed_at and removed_by_id, and a removed assignment is kept as history.
- **R5.** A Unit's member for a role is the open assignment at the nearest node from its UNIT node up to its Sector, or else the program-wide one, or else nobody.
- **R6.** Resolving under R5 skips an assignment whose User is inactive or no longer holds an unrevoked INSTAWORK_ADMIN grant.
- **R7.** A Program User sees the resolved team of every Unit, and a Unit User of each Unit their grants cover, with each member's name, email, and phone.

## Positions and markets

Reference lists every other module prices and filters by.

<a id="req-catalog-0001"></a>

### Hold the Compass Position catalog

`REQ-CATALOG-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin
- **What:** Iris holds one catalog of Positions in Compass's own names, loaded and kept by Instawork Admins. Every Shift, Rate Line, and Credential Requirement names a Position from it.
- **Why:** Every agency names jobs differently; Compass wants one set of titles *(RC-2: Standard Compass position catalog)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-2; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Position list

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only an Instawork Admin adds, renames, deactivates, or reactivates a Position.
- **R2.** Two Positions never share a name.
- **R3.** At each start an empty catalog gets, as active Positions, Server, Banquet server, Bartender, Barback, Line cook, Prep cook, Dishwasher, Food runner, Busser, Cashier, Barista, Concessions attendant, Event staff, Porter, and Housekeeper (I-7).
- **R4.** An inactive Position cannot be chosen for a new Shift or a new Rate Line, and records that already name it are unchanged.
- **R5.** Unit Users and Agency Users choose Positions from the catalog and cannot add one.
- **R6.** A title in a file that equals no Position name is a row problem and never adds a Position.

<a id="req-catalog-0002"></a>

### Hold Markets and their ZIP codes

`REQ-CATALOG-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin
- **What:** A Market is a city in a state, with the ZIP codes that belong to it. Instawork Admins load the pilot's Markets (I-8), and Rate Lines and Units refer to them.
- **Why:** About 200K rates sit in spreadsheets with known inaccuracies *(RC-3: Structured rate card by position, market and vendor, replacing the master spreadsheet)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-3; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §3 Supplier Rates

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only an Instawork Admin adds a Market, renames it, or adds and removes its ZIP codes.
- **R2.** A Market has a city name and a two-letter state, and no two Markets share both.
- **R3.** A ZIP code is five digits and belongs to at most one Market; adding it to a second Market is refused.
- **R4.** Adding a ZIP code to a Market moves the Units with that ZIP code to it through [`REQ-ORG-0002`](#req-org-0002), and removing a ZIP code changes no Unit.

## Agencies

<a id="req-agencies-0001"></a>

### Add an Agency

`REQ-AGENCIES-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User adds each Agency that staffs Compass Shifts. Adding an Agency also invites its first Agency User.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) Creating an agency in bulk

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User adds an Agency.
- **R2.** An Agency needs a name that no other Agency has, and a duplicate name is refused.
- **R3.** Each new Agency needs a first contact with a first name, last name, and email; a phone number is optional.
- **R4.** Adding an Agency invites its contact once through [`REQ-IDENTITY-0002`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-identity-0002) and then grants that User AGENCY_USER for the new Agency through [`REQ-ORG-0005`](#req-org-0005).
- **R7.** A Program User renames, deactivates, or reactivates an Agency; an inactive Agency keeps its records and receives no new Release.

<a id="req-agencies-0002"></a>

### Approve an Agency for part of the org

`REQ-AGENCIES-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User approves an Agency at a Sector, Region, District, or Unit (C-10). Units at or beneath that node can then send it Shifts as a contracted Agency.
- **Why:** Non-compliant spend persists through local relationships *(RC-11: Soft or hard gates for off-contract rates and non-contracted vendors)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-11

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User adds or removes an approval, at a Sector, Region, District, or Unit node, and each approval records who approved it and when.
- **R2.** An approval covers a Unit when it has not been removed and sits at the Unit's node or one of its ancestors.
- **R3.** An Agency with no approval covering a Unit is a non-contracted Agency for that Unit.
- **R4.** An Agency has at most one unremoved approval per org node, and approving it there again is refused.
- **R5.** Removing an approval records who removed it and when, makes the Agency non-contracted for the Units it alone covered, and changes no Release already sent.

<a id="req-agencies-0010"></a>

### Load Agencies from a file

`REQ-AGENCIES-0010`

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User loads many Agencies at once from an AGENCIES file, each with its first Agency User and the org nodes it is approved for. The rows become a Proposal, and nothing is saved until the Program User approves it.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) Creating an agency in bulk; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Uploads

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User sends an AGENCIES file, with one row per Agency.
- **R2.** Each row must give agency, contact_first_name, contact_last_name, and contact_email, and may give contact_phone and approved_for.
- **R3.** Before the Proposal is shown, each row is checked without saving, its contact_phone against [`REQ-IDENTITY-0001.R3`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-identity-0001), its contact_email against [`REQ-IDENTITY-0002.R13`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-identity-0002), and each approved_for name as R5 says, and each failure is a row problem.
- **R4.** A row that repeats an earlier row's agency is reported as a duplicate of that row.
- **R5.** The approved_for column lists org node names separated by semicolons, and a name several org nodes share is a row problem whose candidates show each node with its path.
- **R6.** An accepted row saves its Agency through [`REQ-AGENCIES-0001`](#req-agencies-0001), which invites the contact once and grants them AGENCY_USER, and then approves each approved_for node through [`REQ-AGENCIES-0002`](#req-agencies-0002).
- **R7.** A row whose agency is already an Agency in Iris is a row problem whose fix drops the row, because an AGENCIES file adds Agencies and never changes one.

## Rate cards

What each Agency charges, how rates change, and how deviations are caught.

<a id="req-rates-0001"></a>

### Hold each Agency's Rate Card

`REQ-RATES-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** A Rate Card is one Agency's set of Rate Lines. Each Rate Line prices one Position in one Market, or at one Unit, with Pay and Bill Rates for regular, overtime, and double-time hours.
- **Why:** About 200K rates sit in spreadsheets with known inaccuracies *(RC-3: Structured rate card by position, market and vendor, replacing the master spreadsheet)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-3; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §3 Supplier Rates; [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) Just do % only

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Rate Line names one Agency, one active Position, and exactly one of a Market or a Unit.
- **R2.** A Rate Line holds a Pay Rate and a Bill Rate for each of regular, overtime, and double-time hours, each greater than zero and to the cent.
- **R3.** Each Bill Rate is at least the Pay Rate for the same class of hours.
- **R4.** Overtime rates are at least the regular rates and double-time rates at least the overtime rates, for Pay Rates and for Bill Rates.
- **R5.** A Rate Line has an effective_from date and prices no work dated before it.
- **R6.** Markup is never entered or stored; it is the Bill Rate minus the Pay Rate, divided by the Pay Rate, shown as a percentage (C-14).
- **R7.** A line that fails any of these checks is not saved, and the submitter is told which check failed.
- **R8.** A Unit User sees Bill Rates only, never Pay Rates or Markup, and only on APPROVED lines.
- **R9.** Pay Rates and Markup are shown only to Program Users and to Users of the Agency that owns the line.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0005` See Agencies and their Bill Rates for the Unit](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0005)

- [`REQ-PROGRAM-WEB-0003` List every Agency's Rate Lines and enter rates](program-user.md#req-program-web-0003)

<a id="req-rates-0002"></a>

### Load Rate Lines in bulk

`REQ-RATES-0002`

- **Who:** Agency User, Program User
- **What:** An Agency User or a Program User loads many Rate Lines at once from a RATE_CARD file. The rows become a Proposal, and each accepted row is submitted as a Rate Line.
- **Why:** Needed to load pilot-market rates quickly *(RC-4: Bulk rate upload and import)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-4; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Templates; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Rate Cards & Supplier Sourcing

**Rules**

- **R1.** A RATE_CARD file has one row per Agency, Position, and Market or Unit, and each row must give the position, all six rates, effective_from, and a reason where [`REQ-RATES-0009`](#req-rates-0009) requires one.
- **R2.** An Agency User's rows are for their own Agency, so a row that names another Agency is a row problem; a Program User's rows must name the Agency (C-13).
- **R3.** A row names a Market by city and state, or a Unit by unit; a row that gives both, or neither, is a row problem.
- **R4.** An agency, a city and state, a unit, or a position that does not match exactly one record is a row problem and never creates one.
- **R5.** Markup and ZIP code columns are ignored, because Markup is computed and ZIP codes belong to the Market (C-14).
- **R6.** Each row is checked against [`REQ-RATES-0001`](#req-rates-0001) and the submission rules of [`REQ-RATES-0009`](#req-rates-0009) before the Proposal is shown, and a failing row lists the check it failed.
- **R7.** A row that repeats an earlier row's Agency, Position, Market or Unit, and effective_from is reported as a duplicate of that row.
- **R8.** Each accepted row is submitted through [`REQ-RATES-0009`](#req-rates-0009) in the uploader's name with FILE_UPLOAD as its channel, so it is PENDING for an Agency User and APPROVED for a Program User.
- **R9.** A row that [`REQ-RATES-0009`](#req-rates-0009) would refuse as unchanged is a problem whose suggested fix rejects the row, so loading the same rate card again changes nothing.

<a id="req-rates-0003"></a>

### Keep a history of every rate change

`REQ-RATES-0003` · first slice

- **Who:** Program User, Agency User
- **What:** Every Rate Line ever submitted stays on file with who submitted it, who reviewed it, when, and why it changed. Program Users and the owning Agency can read and download this history.
- **Why:** Know who changed a rate, when and why *(RC-5: Rate change audit trail)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-5

**Rules**

- **R1.** No Rate Line is deleted or overwritten; superseded, PENDING, and SENT_BACK lines all stay in the history.
- **R2.** Each history entry shows who made the change, when, through which channel, the values before and after, and the line's change_reason or end_reason.
- **R3.** A superseded or ended line shows its effective_to and the line that replaced it, when one did.
- **R4.** The history filters by Agency, Position, and Market or Unit.
- **R5.** A Program User sees every Agency's history, and an Agency User sees only their own Agency's.
- **R6.** The history downloads as CSV through [`REQ-INTAKE-0005`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-intake-0005) with only the lines the User may see.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-AGENCY-WEB-0005` Manage the Agency's Rate Card and answer Rate Reviews](agency-user.md#req-agency-web-0005)
- [`REQ-PROGRAM-WEB-0003` List every Agency's Rate Lines and enter rates](program-user.md#req-program-web-0003)

<a id="req-rates-0004"></a>

### Price a Position for one Unit

`REQ-RATES-0004` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** A Rate Line can price a Position at one Unit instead of in a Market. It then applies only to work at that Unit.
- **Why:** Raised; pending a Foodbuy decision *(RC-6: Unit as an additional rate card dimension (position + market + vendor + unit))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-6

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit Rate Line names one Unit that is active when the line is submitted, and no Market.
- **R2.** A Unit Rate Line passes the same checks and the same submission, approval, and effective dating as a Market Rate Line.
- **R3.** A Unit Rate Line replaces only an earlier line for the same Agency, Position, and Unit, never a Market Rate Line.

<a id="req-rates-0005"></a>

### Find the contracted rate

`REQ-RATES-0005` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Given an Agency, a Position, a Unit, and a work date, Iris returns the Rate Line that prices that work, or says that none exists.
- **Why:**
  - Operators don't know the contracted rate when they book *(SC-1: Contracted rate set as default upon booking)*
  - About 200K rates sit in spreadsheets with known inaccuracies *(RC-3: Structured rate card by position, market and vendor, replacing the master spreadsheet)*
  - Raised; pending a Foodbuy decision *(RC-6: Unit as an additional rate card dimension (position + market + vendor + unit))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-1; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-3; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-6

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only APPROVED lines count, and a line is in effect on a date from its effective_from up to but not including its effective_to.
- **R2.** The answer is the line in effect on the work date for that Agency, Position, and Unit, if there is one.
- **R3.** Otherwise it is the line in effect on the work date for that Agency, that Position, and the Unit's Market.
- **R4.** When neither exists the answer is none, meaning the work has no contracted rate.
- **R5.** The work date alone picks the line, so a superseded line still answers for work dated before its effective_to.
- **R6.** The contracted rate is the line's regular Bill Rate, returned with its overtime and double-time Bill Rates and its Pay Rates.

- [D-21](open-questions.md#d-21) What is a Market: a city, a metro, a state, or a set of ZIP codes?

<a id="req-rates-0006"></a>

### Flag rate variance at booking and on Timesheets

`REQ-RATES-0006` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Iris compares the Bill Rates used when a Shift is sent, or billed on a Timesheet, with the contracted rate. A difference is flagged with both rates and the amount.
- **Why:** Units need to see deviations and push back on vendors *(RC-10: Rate variance flags at booking and on approved timesheets, with drill-down (e.g. card $25, paid $29, and why))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-10

**Rules**

- **R1.** Given an Agency, Position, Unit, work date, and Bill Rates, the check compares each given rate with the same rate on the contracted Rate Line.
- **R2.** A given Bill Rate that differs from the contracted one, higher or lower, is a rate variance.
- **R3.** The result names the contracted Rate Line and, for each differing rate, the contracted rate, the rate used, and the difference in dollars.
- **R4.** When no contracted rate exists, the result is off-contract and shows no difference.
- **R6.** The check uses the work date both when a Shift is sent and on its Timesheets, and a variance stays flagged after the Timesheet is approved.
- **R7.** A flag raised when a Shift is sent shows the reason the Unit User gave for the rate (C-16).
- **R8.** Program Users see every rate variance flag, and a Unit User sees the flags on Shifts and Timesheets of the Units their grant covers.

- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0003` Review Timesheets by exception and approve them](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0003)
- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0008` Follow one Shift and change it from its page](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0008)
- [`REQ-PROGRAM-WEB-0011` See every Shift, Release, and Timesheet across the program](program-user.md#req-program-web-0011)

<a id="req-rates-0007"></a>

### Gate off-contract rates and non-contracted Agencies

`REQ-RATES-0007` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** When a Unit sends a Shift, Iris checks the Agency and the Bill Rate against the contract. Two Settings decide whether an off-contract rate or a non-contracted Agency goes ahead with a reason or is refused.
- **Why:** Non-compliant spend persists through local relationships *(RC-11: Soft or hard gates for off-contract rates and non-contracted vendors)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-11

**Rules**

- **R1.** Given a Unit, Agency, Position, work date, and proposed regular Bill Rate, the check returns whether the rate is contracted or off-contract, whether the Agency is non-contracted, and the gate mode for each.
- **R2.** The rate is off-contract when it differs from the contracted rate from [`REQ-RATES-0005`](#req-rates-0005), or when there is no contracted rate.
- **R3.** The Agency is non-contracted when no approval under [`REQ-AGENCIES-0002`](#req-agencies-0002) covers the Unit.
- **R4.** OFF_CONTRACT_RATE_GATE sets the gate mode for an off-contract rate and NON_CONTRACTED_AGENCY_GATE for a non-contracted Agency, each resolved for the Unit and SOFT by default.
- **R5.** Under SOFT the send goes ahead only with a reason from the Unit User, and is flagged as off-contract or non-contracted (C-16).
- **R6.** Under HARD the send is refused, nothing is saved, and the Unit User is told which gate refused it.
- **R7.** Each gate is applied on its own and under SOFT needs its own reason, so a send that trips both goes ahead only if neither is HARD.
- **R8.** A contracted rate sent to an Agency with a covering approval passes with no reason and no flag.
- **R9.** With a Rate Line but a different rate, the check returns overtime and double-time Bill Rates scaled from the line by the ratio of proposed to contracted regular rate, rounded half up to the cent.
- **R10.** With no Rate Line, the Unit User enters the regular Bill Rate, and the check returns overtime at 1.5 times and double time at 2 times it, rounded half up to the cent.
- **R11.** The gates apply only when a Shift is sent, and nothing gates a Timesheet, which bills the rates of its Release.

<a id="req-rates-0008"></a>

### Ask an Agency to review a rate above its peers

`REQ-RATES-0008`

- **Who:** Program User, Agency User
- **What:** Iris flags a regular Bill Rate that is above the Peer Rate by the threshold or more. A Program User can then ask the Agency to lower the rate or justify it.
- **Why:** Units need to see deviations and push back on vendors *(RC-12: Rate review: e.g. when an agency's rates run 15%+ above peer rates, ask the agency to lower the rate or justify it)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-12; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Invoicing & Accruals

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Market Rate Line's Peer Rate is the simple average, rounded half up to the cent, of the regular Bill Rates on other Agencies' APPROVED lines in effect today for the same Position and Market.
- **R2.** A line with no other Agency's line to compare with has no Peer Rate, and a Unit Rate Line has none.
- **R3.** A line in effect today is flagged when its regular Bill Rate is at least the Peer Rate plus PEER_RATE_THRESHOLD_PCT percent of it, a program-wide Setting of 15 by default.
- **R4.** The same comparison is made for any regular Bill Rate, Agency, Position, and Market, so the rate on a Shift can be flagged as above peers when it is sent.
- **R5.** The Peer Rate is shown beside each line to Program Users; an Agency User is told only that a rate is above its peers and never sees the Peer Rate (C-15).
- **R6.** Only a Program User sends a Rate Review, on a flagged line with no REQUESTED review; it is saved as REQUESTED with the Peer Rate at that moment.
- **R7.** RATE_REVIEW_REQUESTED is sent to every active Agency User of the line's Agency, naming the line's Position and Market and saying its rate is above its peers.
- **R8.** An Agency User of that Agency answers a REQUESTED review with a reason to keep the rate, or with a new line for the same Position and Market at a lower regular Bill Rate.
- **R9.** A reason sets the review to KEPT and records the answer, who gave it, and when.
- **R10.** A lower line is submitted through [`REQ-RATES-0009`](#req-rates-0009) and linked to the review with answered_by_id and answered_at; the review becomes LOWERED when the line is APPROVED and stays REQUESTED, open to another answer, if SENT_BACK.
- **R11.** RATE_REVIEW_ANSWERED is sent to the User who requested the review when the Agency gives its reason or submits its lower line, naming the Agency, the Position, the Market, and the answer.
- **R12.** Today, for a Rate Line, is the current date in the program timezone that [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001) names.

<a id="req-rates-0009"></a>

### Submit Rate Lines and approve them before they price work

`REQ-RATES-0009` · first slice

- **Who:** Agency User, Program User
- **What:** Every Rate Line enters Iris through this requirement. An Agency User's line waits as PENDING until a Program User approves it or sends it back, and a Program User's own line is APPROVED at once.
- **Why:**
  - Needed to load pilot-market rates quickly *(RC-4: Bulk rate upload and import)*
  - Know who changed a rate, when and why *(RC-5: Rate change audit trail)*
- **Sources:** [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Rate Cards & Supplier Sourcing; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-4; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-5

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User submits Rate Lines only for their own Agency, and a Program User submits them for any Agency (C-13).
- **R2.** A submitted line must pass every check in [`REQ-RATES-0001`](#req-rates-0001), or it is not saved.
- **R3.** A line an Agency User submits is saved as PENDING, and RATE_LINE_PENDING is sent to every active Program User for each line, including each accepted row of a file.
- **R4.** A line a Program User submits is saved as APPROVED, with no second approval.
- **R5.** Only a Program User approves a PENDING line or sends it back, and sending back requires a reason; either way the line records the reviewer and the time.
- **R6.** When a PENDING line is approved or sent back, RATE_LINE_DECIDED is sent to the User who submitted it, with the reason if it was sent back.
- **R7.** A SENT_BACK line never changes again, and the submitter answers it by submitting a new line.
- **R8.** A line becomes APPROVED only if its effective_from is on or after the effective_from of every APPROVED line for the same Agency, Position, and Market or Unit that prices at least one date.
- **R9.** When a line becomes APPROVED, the APPROVED line in effect on its effective_from for the same Agency, Position, and Market or Unit gets that date as its effective_to, and the new line's replaces_id names it.
- **R10.** Once saved, a line's Agency, Position, Market or Unit, rates, effective_from, and change_reason never change, and its effective_to changes only when a later line replaces it or a Program User ends it.
- **R11.** Each line records who submitted it and the channel it came through.
- **R12.** A line submitted while an APPROVED line exists for the same Agency, Position, and Market or Unit must give a change_reason, or it is not saved; a first line needs none.
- **R13.** A line whose six rates equal those of the APPROVED line in effect on its effective_from for the same Agency, Position, and Market or Unit is refused as unchanged.
- **R14.** A Program User ends an APPROVED line that has no effective_to by setting effective_to on or after its effective_from, with an end_reason; a line ended on its effective_from never prices work.
- **R15.** When a line that answers a Rate Review is approved or sent back, [`REQ-RATES-0008`](#req-rates-0008) updates that review.
- **R16.** A RATE_LINE_PENDING or RATE_LINE_DECIDED message names the line's Agency, Position, Market or Unit, regular Bill Rate, and effective_from, and RATE_LINE_PENDING also names who submitted it.

<a id="req-rates-0013"></a>

### Add or change one Rate Line by form

`REQ-RATES-0013` · first slice

- **Who:** Agency User, Program User
- **What:** An Agency User or a Program User enters one Rate Line by form. Changing a rate means entering a new line that replaces the current one from its effective date.
- **Why:**
  - About 200K rates sit in spreadsheets with known inaccuracies *(RC-3: Structured rate card by position, market and vendor, replacing the master spreadsheet)*
  - Know who changed a rate, when and why *(RC-5: Rate change audit trail)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-3; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-5; [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) Just do % only

**Rules**

- **R1.** The form takes a Position, a Market or a Unit, the six rates, an effective_from date, and a reason; a Program User also picks the Agency.
- **R2.** Saving the form submits the line through [`REQ-RATES-0009`](#req-rates-0009) with the app as its channel.
- **R3.** To change a rate, the form opens filled from the current APPROVED line, and saving submits a new line without editing the old one.
- **R4.** The form shows the Markup of each Pay and Bill Rate pair as a percentage and has no Markup field (C-14).
- **R5.** When a check in [`REQ-RATES-0001`](#req-rates-0001) fails, nothing is submitted and the form names the check.
- **R6.** The reason is required whenever [`REQ-RATES-0009`](#req-rates-0009) requires a change_reason, optional otherwise, and is saved as the new line's change_reason.

## Ordering

How a Unit asks for Workers: Requests, Shifts, Events, and templates.

<a id="req-ordering-0001"></a>

### Create a Request with one or more Shifts

`REQ-ORDERING-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** A Unit User creates a Request for one Unit with one or more Shift lines. Each line becomes a Shift: one Position, from a start time to an end time, for a headcount.
- **Why:** Events need several roles at once *(SC-2: Multiple positions in one request)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-2; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shifts; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) Data Model

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User may create a Request for one Unit, with one or more Shift lines, each for one Position.
- **R2.** Each line states a Position, a date, a start time, an end time, and a headcount, and may state a planned break in minutes and a Department.
- **R3.** Each line becomes one Shift with status OPEN and a line_no that numbers the Request's lines from 1.
- **R4.** starts_at is the line's date and start time, and ends_at its end time on that date or, under R5, on the next.
- **R5.** A Shift must end after it starts; an end time earlier than the start time is offered as ending the next day and saved only after the User confirms that.
- **R6.** A new Shift must end in the future.
- **R7.** Headcount is a whole number of at least 1.
- **R8.** The Position must be active in the Position catalog, and the Department must be an active Department of the same Unit.
- **R9.** A new Shift's parking, entrance, directions, site_contact, and attire start as its Department's defaults unless the Unit User enters other values.
- **R10.** A Request starts in Iris and records its Unit, the User who created it, and created_via, the Channel it came through.
- **R11.** Creating a Request sends nothing to any Agency; a Shift reaches an Agency only through a Release.
- **R12.** A Request cannot be created for a Unit whose org node is inactive.
- **R13.** A start or end time that the clock skips on its date is refused, and one that the clock repeats is read as the earlier of the two.
- **R14.** A line given no Department takes the Position's default Department at the Unit, or the Unit's only active Department; with neither, the line is refused.

<a id="req-ordering-0002"></a>

### Show the contracted rate for each Shift line while booking

`REQ-ORDERING-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** While booking, a Unit User sees the contracted Bill Rate of each Agency a Shift line could go to, before anything is sent. Break and minimum-wage flags show on the line too. The rates a Release is sent at are saved on the Release, not on the Shift.
- **Why:** Operators don't know the contracted rate when they book *(SC-1: Contracted rate set as default upon booking)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-1; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shifts; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Shift Creation

**Rules**

- **R1.** For each Shift line, the Unit User sees every active Agency approved for the Unit with its contracted regular Bill Rate for the line's Position, Unit, and work date, as [`REQ-RATES-0005`](#req-rates-0005) finds it.
- **R2.** An active Agency with no approval covering the Unit can still be picked and is marked non-contracted, and an Agency with no contracted rate for the line shows no rate.
- **R3.** When an Agency is picked for a line, its contracted regular Bill Rate is filled in as the rate the Release will be sent at.
- **R4.** Before sending, the line shows what [`REQ-RATES-0007`](#req-rates-0007) requires for the picked Agency and Bill Rate: nothing, a reason, or that the send is refused.
- **R5.** Each line is also checked by [`REQ-LABOR-0002`](#req-labor-0002), using its times, its planned break, and the picked Agency's regular Pay Rate, and a rule not met shows as a flag that never blocks booking.
- **R6.** Pricing a line saves no rate on the Shift; Bill Rates are saved only on a Release when it is sent.
- **R7.** The caller gives each line's Unit, Position, date, times, and planned break, so a line is priced the same before its Request is saved and after.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0002` Book a Request by form](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0002)
- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0009` Pick an Agency and a rate in one send step](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0009)

**Open questions it rests on**

- [D-17](open-questions.md#d-17) In MVP, can one Shift go to more than one Agency?
- [D-23](open-questions.md#d-23) Do break and minimum-wage checks at booking flag the Shift or block it?

<a id="req-ordering-0003"></a>

### Edit a Shift until it ends and cancel it before it starts

`REQ-ORDERING-0003` · first slice

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** Until a Shift ends, a Unit User can change its headcount, times, and site instructions. Until it starts, they can cancel it. Agencies holding the Shift are told of each change.
- **Why:** Headcounts change constantly and climb as the event nears *(SC-3: Fast edits to open requests (add headcount, change times))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-3; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shift statuses

**Rules**

- **R1.** Until a Shift's ends_at, a Unit User over its Unit may change its headcount, date, start time, end time, planned break, and site instruction fields, unless it is CANCELLED.
- **R2.** An edit is refused unless the changed Shift still passes every check a new Shift must pass.
- **R3.** Headcount cannot be lowered below the total headcount of the Shift's PENDING and ACCEPTED Releases, or below the needed_headcount that [`REQ-ORDERING-0005`](#req-ordering-0005) keeps, when one is set.
- **R4.** When an edit changes the date, times, headcount, or site instructions of a Shift with a PENDING or ACCEPTED Release, SHIFT_CHANGED is sent to the active Agency Users of each Agency holding one.
- **R5.** Until a Shift's starts_at, a Unit User over its Unit may cancel it while it is OPEN, PARTIALLY_FILLED, or FILLED, which sets status CANCELLED, cancelled_by_id, and cancelled_at.
- **R6.** A cancel calls [`REQ-DISPATCH-0001`](#req-dispatch-0001), which cancels the Shift's PENDING and ACCEPTED Releases, and [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0016`](#req-workforce-0016) reacts by removing its ASSIGNED Workers; this requirement changes neither record itself.
- **R7.** A CANCELLED Shift cannot be edited, sent to an Agency, or staffed.
- **R8.** After its ends_at a Shift cannot be edited or cancelled, and changes to the hours worked are made on Timesheets (C-38).
- **R9.** An edit may come from the Shift's page, a SHIFTS file row, a typed request, or a message, and a cancel from any of these except a file (C-39).
- **R10.** A Shift's Unit, Position, and Department never change once it is created; a Shift booked for the wrong one is cancelled and booked again.
- **R16.** When an edit is saved, [`REQ-ORDERING-0006`](#req-ordering-0006) reacts to changed site instructions, [`REQ-ORDERING-0008`](#req-ordering-0008) to a changed headcount, and [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0016`](#req-workforce-0016) to a changed date or time; each owns its rule.
- **R17.** SHIFT_CHANGED is sent once for each PENDING or ACCEPTED Release of the Shift, as its subject, and names the Unit, the Position, the Shift's date, and each changed field with its old and new value.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0008` Follow one Shift and change it from its page](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0008)

<a id="req-ordering-0004"></a>

### Book recurring and chained Shifts

`REQ-ORDERING-0004`

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** One Request can repeat its Shift lines on a weekly pattern until an end date, so recurring needs are not entered again. A multi-week assignment, a chained block, is booked as one such Request.
- **Why:** Recurring needs shouldn't be re-entered *(SC-4: Recurring and chained shifts (multi-week assignments booked as a block))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-4

**Rules**

- **R1.** A recurring Request states recurrence_weekdays, recurrence_every_weeks of at least 1, and recurrence_ends_on, and each line creates one Shift for every matching date from its own date through that end date.
- **R2.** A date matches when it is one of the recurrence_weekdays and falls in a counted seven-day span: the first starts on the line's date, and then every recurrence_every_weeks-th span counts.
- **R3.** Every occurrence is created as a Shift through [`REQ-ORDERING-0001`](#req-ordering-0001) when the Request is created, passes the checks of a new Shift, and has its own status, Releases, and Assignments.
- **R4.** Shifts created from the same line share its line_no and form a series.
- **R5.** A Unit User may apply an edit or a cancel to one Shift or to its whole series, and a series change applies only to the Shifts that have not started.
- **R6.** A chained block, a multi-week assignment, is booked as one recurring Request; Iris stores nothing more for it and treats its Shifts as any series.
- **R7.** A line's date must fall on one of the recurrence_weekdays, and recurrence_ends_on is included, is on or after that date, and is at most 52 weeks after it.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0017` Repeat a Request weekly and act on its series](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0017)

**Open questions it rests on**

- [D-20](open-questions.md#d-20) How does a recurring Request repeat?
- [D-165](open-questions.md#d-165) Does a change to a recurring Shift apply to one Shift or to its series?
- [D-166](open-questions.md#d-166) Must an Agency accept a chained block as a whole and keep the same Workers on every Shift?

<a id="req-ordering-0005"></a>

### Overbook and add headcount on the day

`REQ-ORDERING-0005`

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** A Unit User can book more Workers than needed, such as 55 when 50 are needed, and Iris records both numbers. They can also add headcount on the day, until the Shift ends.
- **Why:** Common at large Levy events *(SC-5: Overbooking and on-the-day add (e.g. 50 needed, 55 arrive))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-5

**Rules**

- **R1.** When booking more Workers than needed, a Unit User sets headcount to the number booked and needed_headcount to the number needed.
- **R2.** needed_headcount is at least 1 and at most headcount; setting it outside that range is refused here, and lowering headcount below it is refused by [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003).
- **R3.** needed_headcount is a record only: Shift status and Releases use headcount, every Worker who works counts toward spend, and no MVP report reads it.
- **R4.** A Unit User may raise a Shift's headcount on the day it is worked, even after it has started, until its ends_at.
- **R5.** Headcount added on the day stays unsent until the Unit User sends it to an Agency through [`REQ-DISPATCH-0001`](#req-dispatch-0001).

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0018` Record the headcount needed when a Unit overbooks](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0018)

**Open questions it rests on**

- [D-18](open-questions.md#d-18) Until when can a Unit change a Shift?
- [D-19](open-questions.md#d-19) When a Unit books more Workers than it needs, such as 55 for 50, which Workers are billed?
- [D-157](open-questions.md#d-157) How is a Shift's headcount shared among its Releases?

<a id="req-ordering-0006"></a>

### Share structured site instructions with the Agency and Workers

`REQ-ORDERING-0006` · first slice

- **Who:** Agency User, Iris
- **What:** Each Shift carries site instructions in five fields: parking, entrance, directions, site contact, and attire. The Agency sees them on its Release, and each assigned Worker receives them by text or email.
- **Why:** VMS requirement: onboarding instructions (attire, directions, parking) *(SC-6: Structured shift instructions shared with the agency and sent to workers by text or email: parking, entrance, directions, site contact, attire)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-6

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Shift's site instructions are its parking, entrance, directions, site_contact, and attire fields, each an optional text.
- **R2.** An Agency User sees the five fields on each PENDING or ACCEPTED Release their Agency holds on the Shift.
- **R3.** When [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003) makes an Assignment ASSIGNED on a Shift that has not ended and has a site instruction filled, SITE_INSTRUCTIONS is sent to the Worker by EMAIL and SMS, whichever addresses the Worker has.
- **R4.** When [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003) changes a site instruction of a Shift that has not ended, SITE_INSTRUCTIONS is sent again to every ASSIGNED Worker on it.
- **R5.** Each send sets instructions_sent_at on the Assignment through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003).
- **R6.** When R3 or R4 would send to a Worker with neither an email nor a phone, nothing is sent, and INSTRUCTIONS_NOT_SENT goes in the app to every active Agency User of the Worker's Agency.
- **R7.** A SITE_INSTRUCTIONS message names the Unit, the Position, and the Shift's date and start and end times, followed by each filled site instruction field; INSTRUCTIONS_NOT_SENT names the Worker and the Shift.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-AGENCY-WEB-0002` List the Releases sent to the Agency and answer them](agency-user.md#req-agency-web-0002)
- [`REQ-AGENCY-WEB-0006` Assign, swap, and remove Workers on an accepted Release](agency-user.md#req-agency-web-0006)

**Open questions it rests on**

- [D-88](open-questions.md#d-88) What happens when an assigned Worker has no email and no phone, so site instructions cannot be sent to them?

<a id="req-ordering-0007"></a>

### Save Request templates and Unit defaults

`REQ-ORDERING-0007`

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** A Unit User saves Request templates, such as a game-day package of 5 bartenders and 4 concessions workers. They also set the Department each Position defaults to, which prefills new Requests.
- **Why:** Entering requests is slow and repetitive *(SC-11: Request templates and location defaults (e.g. game-day package: 5 bartenders, 4 concessions))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-11

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User over a Unit may create, change, and delete its Request templates, each with a name that is unique within the Unit.
- **R2.** A template line holds an active Position, a headcount of at least 1, a start time, and an end time, and may hold a Department of the Unit and a planned break.
- **R3.** A template line whose end time is before its start time is saved only after the User confirms that it ends the next day.
- **R4.** Applying a template to a date fills a new Request with one Shift line per template line, and the Unit User may change any line before creating it.
- **R5.** A Request made from a template is created through [`REQ-ORDERING-0001`](#req-ordering-0001) as any other Request is, so changing or deleting the template later changes no Request.
- **R6.** A Unit User over a Unit may set one default Department for each Position there, and a new Shift line for that Position is prefilled with it.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0011` Keep Request templates and the Unit's booking defaults](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0011)

<a id="req-ordering-0008"></a>

### Keep each Shift's status in step with its Workers and the clock

`REQ-ORDERING-0008` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Iris sets each Shift's status from its ASSIGNED Workers, its headcount, and the clock. No User sets a status by hand.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shift statuses

**Rules**

- **R1.** Before its ends_at, a Shift that is not CANCELLED is OPEN with no ASSIGNED Worker, PARTIALLY_FILLED with fewer than its headcount, and FILLED with its headcount or more.
- **R2.** When [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003) makes an Assignment ASSIGNED or REMOVED, or [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003) changes a Shift's headcount, the status of that Shift, if it has not ended, is set again under R1.
- **R3.** An interval job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001) sets each PARTIALLY_FILLED or FILLED Shift whose ends_at has passed to WORKED.
- **R4.** The same job sets each OPEN Shift whose ends_at has passed to UNFILLED.
- **R5.** When [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003) assigns a Worker from a Timesheet to an UNFILLED Shift, the Shift becomes WORKED.
- **R6.** A CANCELLED Shift never changes status, and a WORKED Shift stays WORKED.
- **R7.** No User can set a Shift's status directly.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0007` List the Unit's Shifts by date](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0007)
- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0008` Follow one Shift and change it from its page](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0008)
- [`REQ-AGENCY-WEB-0007` Manage one Worker's Credentials and Attestations](agency-user.md#req-agency-web-0007)
- [`REQ-PROGRAM-WEB-0011` See every Shift, Release, and Timesheet across the program](program-user.md#req-program-web-0011)

- [D-67](open-questions.md#d-67) How often does timed work run?
- [D-164](open-questions.md#d-164) Can a Worker be added to a Shift after it ends?

<a id="req-ordering-0009"></a>

### Draft a Request from a plain-language sentence

`REQ-ORDERING-0009`

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** A Unit User types what they need in the assistant, such as “3 bartenders and 2 line cooks Monday”. Iris drafts the Request as a Proposal for them to review, change, and approve.
- **Why:** Faster than forms; handles partial info and asks for what's missing *(SC-9: Natural-language booking in the app ("3 bartenders and 2 line cooks Monday"))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-9; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 Agent Chat; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Shift Creation

**Rules**

- **R1.** From the text, Iris reads each line's Position, headcount, Unit, date, and start and end times.
- **R2.** When the User's scope covers several Units and the text names none, Iris asks which Unit before drafting.
- **R3.** When the text names no Agency, Iris lists the Agencies approved for the Unit with their contracted Bill Rates and asks which should receive each line.
- **R4.** The draft is a Proposal of kind REQUEST_DRAFT that shows each Shift line, its Agency, and its Bill Rate as [`REQ-ORDERING-0002`](#req-ordering-0002) prices it.
- **R5.** Each drafted line is checked as a new Shift is, and a line that fails shows its problem in the draft.
- **R6.** The User may change any line of the draft before approving it.
- **R7.** On approval, the Request and its Shifts are created through [`REQ-ORDERING-0001`](#req-ordering-0001) with created_via ASSISTANT, and each line with an Agency is sent through [`REQ-DISPATCH-0001`](#req-dispatch-0001).
- **R8.** A drafted line is sent only at the contracted rate: an Agency with no contracted rate is a problem, and a non-contracted Agency needs a reason the User adds by editing the line.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-ASSISTANT-0003` Hand each typed request to the requirement that owns it](every-user.md#req-assistant-0003)

**Open questions it rests on**

- [D-17](open-questions.md#d-17) In MVP, can one Shift go to more than one Agency?

<a id="req-ordering-0010"></a>

### Take Requests and Shift changes by email, SMS, or phone

`REQ-ORDERING-0010`

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** A Unit User can order by email, text, or phone call. Iris drafts the Request, fills gaps from what the Unit ordered before, and creates nothing until the sender confirms on the same channel. A message that asks to change or cancel a Shift is drafted the same way.
- **Why:** About 30% of Instawork shifts already come in through chat *(SC-10: Booking by email, SMS and phone through an AI agent, with memory of each unit's preferences)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-10

**Rules**

- **R1.** An email, text, or call that [`REQ-MESSAGING-0002`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-messaging-0002) matched to a Unit User and that asks for Workers is drafted the way [`REQ-ORDERING-0009`](#req-ordering-0009) drafts typed text.
- **R2.** When the message leaves out the times, Department, or Agency for a Position, Iris fills them from the Shift most recently created at the Unit for that Position that is not CANCELLED.
- **R3.** The draft goes back to the sender on the channel they used, and for an email or a text a reply in the same thread approves or rejects it, as [`REQ-MESSAGING-0002`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-messaging-0002) provides.
- **R4.** On approval, the Request is created with created_via EMAIL, SMS, or PHONE, and each line with an Agency is sent through [`REQ-DISPATCH-0001`](#req-dispatch-0001).
- **R5.** On a call, the AI agent reads the draft aloud, and the caller's spoken yes approves it and spoken no rejects it on that call, as a reply does in a thread.
- **R6.** A matched Unit User's message that asks to change or cancel a Shift is drafted as [`REQ-ORDERING-0015`](#req-ordering-0015) drafts a typed request, and is answered and approved as a booking is.
- **R7.** A message has no session: its sender acts as UNIT_USER across their unrevoked UNIT_USER grants, which [`REQ-ORG-0009`](#req-org-0009) checks, and a sender with none is refused with that reason.
- **R8.** The Agency is filled only when every Release of that Shift went to the same Agency, and otherwise Iris asks as [`REQ-ORDERING-0009.R3`](#req-ordering-0009) does.
- **R9.** The draft marks each value filled from an earlier Shift.

**Open questions it rests on**

- [D-17](open-questions.md#d-17) In MVP, can one Shift go to more than one Agency?
- [D-48](open-questions.md#d-48) What does Iris remember about each Unit when it books by email, SMS, or phone?
- [D-93](open-questions.md#d-93) Does a spoken yes on a call approve a draft?
- [D-209](open-questions.md#d-209) Which changes to a Shift can a typed request or a message make?
- [D-238](open-questions.md#d-238) In which role does the sender of an email, text, or call act?

<a id="req-ordering-0011"></a>

### Group Shifts into an Event

`REQ-ORDERING-0011`

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** A Unit User names an Event, such as a Friday banquet, and attaches Shifts to it, so the Event's cost can be seen as one.
- **Why:** Units want to know what last Friday's banquet actually cost, and some clients expect it the next morning *(REP-2: Event-level cost: group shifts into an event and see projected vs. actual, available the next morning)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-2

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User over a Unit may create and rename Events for it, and an Event's name is unique within the Unit.
- **R2.** A Unit User may attach a Shift to one Event of the Shift's own Unit, move it to another, or detach it, whatever the Shift's status.
- **R3.** A Shift belongs to at most one Event, and the Shifts of one Request may belong to different Events.
- **R4.** Each attach, move, or detach of a Shift is published as an event, to which [`REQ-TIPS-0004`](#req-tips-0004) reacts under its own rules.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-UNIT-WEB-0010` Name Events and see each Event's projected and actual cost](unit-user.md#req-unit-web-0010)
- [`REQ-AGENCY-WEB-0004` List the Agency's Timesheets and submit them](agency-user.md#req-agency-web-0004)

**Open questions it rests on**

- [D-242](open-questions.md#d-242) What happens to a Tip Pool entered for an Event when a Shift is later attached to that Event, moved to another, or detached from it?

<a id="req-ordering-0014"></a>

### Load Shifts from a file

`REQ-ORDERING-0014`

- **Who:** Unit User, Agency User
- **What:** A Unit User uploads a SHIFTS file to create or change many Shifts at once. An Agency User uploads one to assign named Workers to Shifts released to their Agency.
- **Why:**
  - Events need several roles at once *(SC-2: Multiple positions in one request)*
  - VMS requirement: onboarding instructions (attire, directions, parking) *(SC-6: Structured shift instructions shared with the agency and sent to workers by text or email: parking, entrance, directions, site contact, attire)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-2; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-6; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Templates; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 What the agent checks

**Rules**

- **R1.** Each row of a SHIFTS file becomes a Proposal item under [`REQ-INTAKE-0002`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-intake-0002) that creates a Shift, changes a Shift, or assigns a Worker.
- **R2.** A Unit User's row with no shift_id creates a Shift at a Unit in their scope through [`REQ-ORDERING-0001`](#req-ordering-0001), with created_via set to the Proposal's channel.
- **R3.** The rows of one file that create Shifts at the same Unit share one group_key and form one Request.
- **R4.** A Unit User's row with a shift_id changes that Shift's date, times, break, headcount, or site instructions through [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003) and its Event through [`REQ-ORDERING-0011`](#req-ordering-0011); an empty column changes nothing.
- **R5.** A change row is refused when [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003) does not allow that change in the Shift's current status.
- **R6.** A row that creates a Shift must give a unit, position, date, start_time, end_time, and headcount, and a row that assigns a Worker must give the Worker's first and last name.
- **R7.** On a row that creates a Shift, an agency value sends the Shift's whole headcount to that Agency through [`REQ-DISPATCH-0001`](#req-dispatch-0001) at the contracted rate, under that requirement's checks.
- **R8.** An Agency User's row assigns the person it names through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003) to the Agency's ACCEPTED Release on its shift_id, and a person who matches no Worker of the Agency is proposed as a new Worker.
- **R9.** An Agency User's row cannot create or change a Shift, and a Unit User's row cannot assign a Worker.
- **R10.** The unit, position, and agency are looked up by name, and the department and event by name within the row's Unit.
- **R11.** The date, start_time, and end_time are checked as a new Shift's are, and a filled parking, entrance, directions, site_contact, or attire column replaces that default.
- **R12.** A row that would create a Shift with the same Unit, Position, Department, start, and end as an earlier row, or as a Shift that is not CANCELLED, is reported as a duplicate.
- **R13.** A shift_id that matches no Shift the uploader may act on is a problem with no suggested fix.
- **R14.** shift_id is the Shift's id, which every downloaded list of Shifts or Releases carries, so its rows can be changed and uploaded again as a SHIFTS file.
- **R15.** On a row with a shift_id, a unit, position, or department that differs from the Shift's is a problem, and the agency column is not read.
- **R16.** A row whose agency has no contracted rate for the new Shift is a problem whose fix clears the agency, because a file carries no Bill Rate.
- **R17.** A row whose agency is non-contracted needs a non_contracted_reason where [`REQ-RATES-0007`](#req-rates-0007) answers SOFT and is a problem where it answers HARD; both are found before the Proposal is shown.
- **R18.** A row with no date, where every other row of the file for the same Event gives one date, is a problem whose fix is that date.
- **R19.** The person an Agency User's row names is matched under [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0002`](#req-workforce-0002), and a proposed new Worker is created through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0001`](#req-workforce-0001) from the row's name, email, and phone when the row is accepted.
- **R20.** Before the Proposal is shown, a row that assigns a matched Worker is checked under [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003.R26`](#req-workforce-0003), and each reason it would be refused is a row problem.

<a id="req-ordering-0015"></a>

### Change or cancel Shifts by a typed request

`REQ-ORDERING-0015`

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** A Unit User types a change to a Shift's headcount or times, or asks to cancel it. Iris drafts the change as a Proposal, and the Shift changes only when the Unit User approves it.
- **Why:** Headcounts change constantly and climb as the event nears *(SC-3: Fast edits to open requests (add headcount, change times))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-3; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 Who uses it; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 Agent Chat

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User's typed request to change a Shift's headcount or times, or to cancel it, becomes a Proposal of kind SHIFT_CHANGE with one item for each Shift it names.
- **R2.** Iris finds each Shift the request means among the Shifts in the User's scope that have not ended, from the Unit, Position, date, and start time it gives.
- **R3.** When no Shift or several match, or the new headcount or time is missing, Iris asks under [`REQ-AGENT-0003`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-agent-0003) and creates no Proposal until the User answers.
- **R4.** Each item shows the Shift's current values beside the change or the cancel, is checked without saving against the rules of [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003) when drafted, and shows its problem when a check fails.
- **R5.** On apply, each accepted item is saved as an edit or a cancel through [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003), so SHIFT_CHANGED and the cancel's effects follow as they do from the Shift's page.
