## Dispatch

How a Shift reaches Agencies and how they answer.

<a id="req-dispatch-0001"></a>

### Send a Shift's headcount to a chosen Agency

`REQ-DISPATCH-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Unit User, Iris
- **What:** A Unit User picks one Agency and sends it some or all of a Shift's headcount. Each send is a Release that stores the Bill Rates it was sent at, and the Agency is notified.
- **Why:**
  - Agreed starting flow: a unit posts a shift, then the agency assigns a worker *(SC-7: Send each request to a chosen agency)*
  - Operators don't know the contracted rate when they book *(SC-1: Contracted rate set as default upon booking)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-7; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-1; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) Data Model; [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) a single agency, then request worker as a nested feature; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User over the Unit of a Shift that is not CANCELLED may send any part of its unsent headcount to one active Agency they choose, creating a PENDING Release with released_by_id and released_at.
- **R2.** Unsent headcount is the Shift's headcount less the headcounts of its PENDING and ACCEPTED Releases; a Release's headcount is at least 1 and never more than the unsent headcount.
- **R3.** A new Release can be sent until the Shift starts; from then until its ends_at, headcount can only be added to an ACCEPTED Release.
- **R4.** Sending more headcount to an Agency that already holds a PENDING or ACCEPTED Release on the Shift raises that Release's headcount and keeps its status and rates, so an ACCEPTED Release is not answered again.
- **R5.** The Release stores rate_line_id and the regular, overtime, and double-time Bill Rates of the contracted Rate Line that [`REQ-RATES-0005`](#req-rates-0005) finds for the Agency, Position, Unit, and work date.
- **R6.** A Unit User may enter another regular Bill Rate with a bill_rate_reason, and the Release then stores the overtime and double-time Bill Rates that [`REQ-RATES-0007`](#req-rates-0007) returns for it.
- **R7.** With no contracted Rate Line, rate_line_id is empty, the Unit User enters the regular Bill Rate and a bill_rate_reason, and the other two rates are those [`REQ-RATES-0007`](#req-rates-0007) returns.
- **R8.** Before a Release is saved, or headcount is added to one, [`REQ-RATES-0007`](#req-rates-0007) checks its Agency and regular Bill Rate under OFF_CONTRACT_RATE_GATE and NON_CONTRACTED_AGENCY_GATE, and a send it refuses saves nothing.
- **R9.** is_non_contracted is set true when [`REQ-RATES-0007`](#req-rates-0007) finds no approval covering the Unit, and the reason it then requires is stored in non_contracted_reason, apart from any bill_rate_reason.
- **R10.** A Release keeps the rates it was sent at when Rate Lines change later.
- **R11.** Creating a Release, or raising its headcount, sends RELEASE_NEW to the Agency's active Agency Users, naming the Unit, the Position, the Shift's date and times, and the Release's headcount.
- **R12.** A Unit User over the Unit may withdraw a PENDING Release, which becomes WITHDRAWN with closed_at set and sends RELEASE_WITHDRAWN to the Agency's active Agency Users.
- **R13.** When [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003) cancels a Shift, it calls this requirement, which sets each of the Shift's PENDING and ACCEPTED Releases to CANCELLED with closed_at and sends RELEASE_WITHDRAWN to each Agency's active Agency Users.
- **R14.** The headcount of a DECLINED, WITHDRAWN, or EXPIRED Release is unsent again and can be sent in a new Release.
- **R15.** Several Shifts of one Request, such as a block, can be sent to one Agency in one step, and each Shift's Release is saved on its own, so a refused Shift stops no other.
- **R16.** A send asked for by a SHIFTS file row or an approved assistant draft is saved by this requirement under the same checks.
- **R18.** A RELEASE_WITHDRAWN message names the Unit, the Position, the Shift's date and times, the Release's headcount, and whether the Release was withdrawn or its Shift cancelled.
- **R19.** When headcount is added to a Release and a SOFT gate needs a reason the Release does not hold, the send must give it, and it is stored on the Release.

<a id="req-dispatch-0002"></a>

### Accept or decline a Release

`REQ-DISPATCH-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Agency User, Iris
- **What:** An Agency User accepts or declines each Release sent to their Agency, and the Unit User who sent it is told. A Release nobody answers expires when the Shift starts.
- **Why:** Agencies are half the users; they need to know the moment a shift is theirs *(SC-8: Agency notifications for released shifts (email or SMS), with accept or decline)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-8; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Shift Creation

**Rules**

- **R1.** Before the Shift starts, an Agency User of the Release's Agency may accept a PENDING Release, which becomes ACCEPTED with responded_by_id and responded_at.
- **R2.** Before the Shift starts, an Agency User of the Release's Agency may decline a PENDING Release with a decline_reason, which becomes DECLINED with responded_by_id and responded_at.
- **R3.** An answer covers the Release's whole headcount; an Agency cannot accept part of it.
- **R4.** Until the Shift starts, an Agency User may decline an ACCEPTED Release with a decline_reason; it becomes DECLINED with responded_by_id and responded_at set again, and [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0016`](#req-workforce-0016) then removes its ASSIGNED Workers.
- **R5.** An interval job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001) sets each Release still PENDING once its Shift's starts_at has passed to EXPIRED with closed_at set.
- **R6.** Only an answer, a withdrawal, a cancellation, or the Shift's start ends a PENDING Release; release windows between Agencies are Phase 2.
- **R7.** Each accept and each decline, including one after accepting, sends RELEASE_ANSWERED to the User who sent the Release, naming the Agency, the Shift's Unit, Position, date, and times, the answer, and any decline_reason.
- **R8.** An Agency User may answer several PENDING Releases in one step, such as those of a block, and each Release is accepted or declined on its own.
- **R9.** An Agency User sees the Shift's whole headcount, their own Release's headcount, whether any other Agency holds a PENDING or ACCEPTED Release on the Shift, and the total headcount those hold.
- **R10.** An Agency User never sees which other Agencies hold the Shift, or their rates, answers, or Workers.

## Workers

Agency Workers, who is assigned where, and Unit feedback on them.

<a id="req-workforce-0001"></a>

### Hold each Agency's Worker roster

`REQ-WORKFORCE-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Agency User
- **What:** Each Agency keeps its Workers in Iris. A Worker belongs to one Agency, so one person at two Agencies is two Workers.
- **Why:** Compass needs to know who is actually coming on site *(WA-1: Agency roster: agencies assign named workers to allocated shifts)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-1; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §4 Professionals; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Templates

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User may add a Worker to their own Agency, and created_via records the Channel the Worker came through.
- **R2.** A Worker needs a first name and a last name; email, phone, city, Positions, and photo are optional.
- **R3.** Within one Agency no two Workers share an email or share a phone, and a save that would break this is refused.
- **R4.** A Worker belongs to exactly one Agency, and the same person at two Agencies is two Workers.
- **R6.** A requirement that reads a name from a file or a typed request and matches no Worker of the Agency creates the Worker here, with a first and last name, once the User approves.
- **R7.** An Agency User may change the details of their Agency's Workers and set is_active to false or true; an inactive Worker cannot be assigned.
- **R8.** A Worker's Positions are informational and do not limit the Shifts the Worker can be assigned to.
- **R10.** A Unit User sees a Worker's name, photo, and Agency, and never their email or phone.
- **R11.** When a Worker is made inactive, [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0016`](#req-workforce-0016) reacts by taking them off the Shifts they are assigned to that have not started; this requirement changes no Assignment.
- **R13.** A Worker's phone is accepted in the forms [`REQ-IDENTITY-0001.R3`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-identity-0001) accepts.
- **R14.** A photo is a JPEG or PNG file stored through [`REQ-INTAKE-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-intake-0001), and photo_url holds its reference.
- **R15.** A Worker's photo may be opened only by an Agency User of the Worker's Agency, a Program User, and a Unit User who sees the Worker under R10.

<a id="req-workforce-0002"></a>

### Match a named person to an existing Worker

`REQ-WORKFORCE-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** When a file, a message, or a form names a person, Iris looks for that person among one Agency's Workers in a fixed order before anyone new is created.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §4 How the system matches a professional

**Rules**

- **R1.** Matching looks only at the Workers of the one Agency the row or message is for.
- **R2.** A named person with the same email as a Worker is that Worker.
- **R3.** Otherwise, a named person with the same phone number as a Worker, once it is put in the stored form, is that Worker.
- **R4.** Otherwise, a Worker with the same first and last name is only a possible match, which the person approving must confirm or reject; Iris never matches on name alone.
- **R5.** The candidates offered are each Worker of the Agency with that name and, where the caller may create one, a new Worker; the person approving picks one under [`REQ-AGENT-0002.R20`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-agent-0002).
- **R6.** With no match, the caller proposes a new Worker from the named person's details, and none is created until a person approves.

**Open questions it rests on**

- [D-225](open-questions.md#d-225) Which names does Iris offer when a name matches no record, or several?

<a id="req-workforce-0003"></a>

### Assign named Workers to an accepted Release

`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003` · first slice

- **Who:** Agency User, Iris
- **What:** An Agency User assigns their Agency's own Workers to a Shift through a Release it accepted, and can swap or remove them. The Unit sees each assigned Worker by name, with their Agency.
- **Why:** Compass needs to know who is actually coming on site *(WA-1: Agency roster: agencies assign named workers to allocated shifts)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-1; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shifts; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User may assign a Worker of their own Agency to a Shift only through their Agency's ACCEPTED Release on it, until the Shift's ends_at.
- **R2.** A Release never holds more ASSIGNED Workers than its headcount, and a Worker has at most one ASSIGNED Assignment on a Shift.
- **R3.** An assignment is refused, with the reason shown, when the Worker is inactive, belongs to another Agency, or is rated BLOCK by the Shift's Unit.
- **R4.** An assignment is refused when [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0005`](#req-compliance-0005) does not find the Worker eligible for the Shift, and the Credential Types not met are shown.
- **R5.** Before an assignment is saved, [`REQ-LABOR-0003`](#req-labor-0003) is given the Worker's ASSIGNED Shifts at every Unit with work dates within six days of this Shift's, at scheduled minutes less planned breaks, with and without this Shift.
- **R6.** When [`REQ-LABOR-0003`](#req-labor-0003) answers to refuse, as [`REQ-LABOR-0003.R6`](#req-labor-0003) says it does for overtime under OVERTIME_HARD_BLOCK, the assignment is not saved; otherwise it is saved.
- **R7.** Workers are assigned in the app, by SHIFTS file rows, or by a typed request under [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0018`](#req-workforce-0018); every channel passes the same checks, and assigned_via records it.
- **R8.** A caller that assigns from a file or a typed request passes the Worker it matched, or created through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0001`](#req-workforce-0001), and this requirement matches no name.
- **R9.** Until the Shift's ends_at, an Agency User may remove their Agency's ASSIGNED Worker; the Assignment becomes REMOVED with REMOVED_BY_AGENCY, removed_by_id, and removed_at.
- **R10.** An Agency User may swap an ASSIGNED Worker for another in one step: the old Assignment becomes REMOVED with SWAPPED, removed_by_id, removed_at, and replaced_by_id, and the new one must pass every check.
- **R16.** WORKER_ASSIGNED goes to every active Unit User over the Shift's Unit when an Assignment becomes ASSIGNED, and WORKER_REMOVED when one becomes REMOVED for any reason except SHIFT_CANCELLED or NOT_ELIGIBLE.
- **R17.** Unit Users over the Shift's Unit see each ASSIGNED Worker's name and Agency.
- **R19.** instructions_sent_at holds the time the Shift's site instructions were last sent to the Worker for that Assignment.
- **R20.** After a Shift ends, a Worker is assigned only when a Timesheet names a Worker of the Agency who has no Assignment on it, and that Assignment may exceed the Release's headcount.
- **R21.** When [`REQ-LABOR-0003`](#req-labor-0003) allows an assignment that adds overtime, the answer to the assigning User names each Unit and Work Week it adds overtime in, because OVERTIME_ALERT is not sent to the User who caused it.
- **R22.** For BLOCKED_BY_UNIT, WORKER_REMOVED also goes to every active Agency User of the Worker's Agency, because the Agency did not cause that removal.
- **R23.** [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0016`](#req-workforce-0016) takes Workers off Shifts through this requirement, giving the removal_reason; such a removal sets removed_at, leaves removed_by_id empty, and follows R16 and R22.
- **R24.** When the assigned Worker has neither an email nor a phone, the answer to the assigning User says so, because INSTRUCTIONS_NOT_SENT is not sent to the User whose action caused it.
- **R25.** When an Assignment becomes ASSIGNED, [`REQ-ORDERING-0006`](#req-ordering-0006), [`REQ-ORDERING-0008`](#req-ordering-0008), [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0006`](#req-compliance-0006), and [`REQ-TIME-0001`](#req-time-0001) each react under their own rules, as [`REQ-ORDERING-0008`](#req-ordering-0008) does when one becomes REMOVED; this requirement calls none of them.
- **R26.** Asked about a Worker and a Release without assigning, this requirement answers whether R1 to R6 would refuse the assignment and why, and saves nothing.
- **R27.** WORKER_ASSIGNED and WORKER_REMOVED have the Assignment's Release as subject and name the Worker, their Agency, the Shift's Unit, Position, date, and times, and, for a removal, the removal_reason.

**Screens that use it**

<a id="req-workforce-0004"></a>

### Request specific Workers by name

`REQ-WORKFORCE-0004`

- **Who:** Unit User, Agency User
- **What:** When sending a Shift to an Agency, a Unit User can name the Workers they want from that Agency. The Agency sees who was asked for and says when one cannot work.
- **Why:** Favorite rosters must carry over (one operator always requests the same 20 people) *(WA-2: Request specific workers, linked to the worker record)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-2; [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) a single agency, then request worker as a nested feature; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User over a Shift's Unit may name Workers they want on it, each saved as a WorkerRequest with status REQUESTED and requested_by_id.
- **R2.** A Worker can be requested only while their Agency holds a PENDING or ACCEPTED Release on the Shift, so a request sits inside the send to one Agency.
- **R3.** A Worker who is inactive, or rated BLOCK by the Shift's Unit, cannot be requested, and a Worker is requested at most once for a Shift.
- **R4.** When picking, the Unit User sees the Agency's active Workers, with those the Unit rated FAVORITE listed first.
- **R5.** Agency Users see the requested Workers marked and listed first when assigning, and may still assign other Workers.
- **R6.** An Agency User of the Worker's Agency may mark a REQUESTED WorkerRequest UNAVAILABLE with an unavailable_reason.
- **R7.** Until the Shift starts, a Unit User over its Unit may withdraw a WorkerRequest in either status, which deletes it.
- **R8.** A WorkerRequest is shown, and can be marked, only while the Worker's Agency holds a PENDING or ACCEPTED Release on the Shift, and it keeps its status when that Release closes.

<a id="req-workforce-0005"></a>

### Rate a Worker as Favorite, Okay to return, or Block

`REQ-WORKFORCE-0005` · first slice

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** A Unit User rates a Worker for one Unit as Favorite, Okay to return, or Block, with an optional review. The rating holds for that Worker at that Unit until it is changed.
- **Why:** Operators want to rate workers and keep the good ones *(WA-3: Post-shift ratings: favorite, okay to return, block)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-3; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §4 Professionals

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User over a Unit may rate a Worker FAVORITE, OKAY_TO_RETURN, or BLOCK for that Unit, with an optional written review.
- **R2.** A Unit holds one current rating per Worker; rating again replaces it and sets rated_by_id and rated_at.
- **R3.** A Worker can be rated before working a Shift at the Unit, so a Unit's existing favorite and block lists can be entered, one Worker at a time.
- **R4.** A rating applies only at the Unit that gave it, and only to that Worker of that Agency.
- **R5.** Agency Users see the ratings and reviews of their own Agency's Workers, and Program Users see every rating.
- **R6.** Saving a BLOCK rating is the event [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0016`](#req-workforce-0016) reacts to by taking the Worker off that Unit's Shifts that have not started; this requirement changes no Assignment.

<a id="req-workforce-0006"></a>

### Report a Worker issue to the Agency

`REQ-WORKFORCE-0006`

- **Who:** Unit User, Agency User
- **What:** A Unit User reports an issue with a Worker, such as conduct, safety, quality, or a no-show. The Worker's Agency receives it and resolves it with a note the Unit can see.
- **Why:** VMS requirement: report associate issues *(WA-4: Report an associate issue (conduct, safety, quality, no-show) routed to the agency, with resolution tracking)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-4

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User over a Unit may report an issue on a Worker for that Unit, with a category of CONDUCT, SAFETY, QUALITY, or NO_SHOW, a description, and optionally a Shift of that Unit.
- **R2.** A new issue has status OPEN and reported_by_id, and WORKER_ISSUE_REPORTED is sent to the active Agency Users of the Worker's Agency, naming the Worker, the Unit, and the category.
- **R3.** An Agency User of the Worker's Agency may resolve an OPEN issue with a resolution note, which sets status RESOLVED, resolved_by_id, and resolved_at.
- **R4.** Resolving an issue sends WORKER_ISSUE_RESOLVED to the User who reported it, naming the Worker, the category, and the resolution note.
- **R5.** Unit Users over the Unit and Agency Users of the Worker's Agency see the issue, its status, and its resolution.

<a id="req-workforce-0016"></a>

### Take Workers off Shifts automatically and recheck their eligibility

`REQ-WORKFORCE-0016` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Iris takes assigned Workers off a Shift when it is cancelled, their Release is declined, the Unit blocks them, their Agency makes them inactive, or they stop being eligible. A job rechecks eligibility each day, and another records it once the Shift starts.
- **Why:** Operators want to rate workers and keep the good ones *(WA-3: Post-shift ratings: favorite, okay to return, block)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-3; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shift statuses; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance

**Rules**

- **R1.** When [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003) cancels a Shift, each of its ASSIGNED Assignments is removed with SHIFT_CANCELLED.
- **R2.** When [`REQ-DISPATCH-0002`](#req-dispatch-0002) declines an ACCEPTED Release, each of its ASSIGNED Assignments is removed with RELEASE_DECLINED.
- **R3.** When [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0005`](#req-workforce-0005) saves a BLOCK rating, the Worker's ASSIGNED Assignments on that Unit's Shifts that have not started are removed with BLOCKED_BY_UNIT.
- **R4.** When [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0001`](#req-workforce-0001) makes a Worker inactive, the Worker's ASSIGNED Assignments on Shifts that have not started are removed with WORKER_INACTIVE.
- **R5.** A daily job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001), at 06:00 in each Unit's timezone, asks [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0005`](#req-compliance-0005) again about every ASSIGNED Worker on that Unit's Shifts that have not started.
- **R6.** When [`REQ-ORDERING-0003`](#req-ordering-0003) changes the date or times of a Shift that has not started, [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0005`](#req-compliance-0005) is asked again at once about every ASSIGNED Worker on it.
- **R7.** When either recheck finds an ASSIGNED Worker not eligible, the Assignment is removed with NOT_ELIGIBLE, and [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0005`](#req-compliance-0005) sends WORKER_NOT_ELIGIBLE.
- **R8.** Every removal here is made through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003), which records the reason and sends WORKER_REMOVED where its rules say.
- **R9.** An interval job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001) records is_eligible_at_start, from [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0005`](#req-compliance-0005)'s answer at that run, on each ASSIGNED Assignment that has none on a Shift whose starts_at has passed.

<a id="req-workforce-0017"></a>

### Load Workers from a file

`REQ-WORKFORCE-0017`

- **Who:** Agency User
- **What:** An Agency User loads many Workers at once from a WORKERS file. Each row is matched to the Agency's Workers, and the rows become a Proposal that adds or changes Workers once the Agency User approves it.
- **Why:** Compass needs to know who is actually coming on site *(WA-1: Agency roster: agencies assign named workers to allocated shifts)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-1; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Templates; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §4 How the system matches a professional

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only an Agency User sends a WORKERS file, with one row for each Worker of their own Agency.
- **R2.** Each WORKERS row is matched under [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0002`](#req-workforce-0002); a row that matches an existing Worker proposes changes to that Worker, and only an unmatched row proposes a new one.
- **R3.** In a WORKERS row, positions are looked up by Position name, separated by semicolons, and a name that matches no Position is a problem.
- **R4.** Two WORKERS rows are duplicates when they share an email or share a phone, and the later row is the duplicate.
- **R5.** Before the Proposal is shown, each row is checked, without saving, against [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0001.R2`](#req-workforce-0001), R3, and R13 as the Worker it would add or change, and each failure is a row problem.
- **R6.** An accepted row adds or changes its Worker through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0001`](#req-workforce-0001), and a new Worker's created_via is the Proposal's channel.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-AGENCY-WEB-0013` Upload Workers from the roster](agency-user.md#req-agency-web-0013)

<a id="req-workforce-0018"></a>

### Assign Workers by a typed request

`REQ-WORKFORCE-0018`

- **Who:** Agency User
- **What:** An Agency User types which Workers to put on a Shift released to their Agency. Iris drafts the Assignments as a Proposal, and nobody is assigned until the Agency User approves it.
- **Why:** Compass needs to know who is actually coming on site *(WA-1: Agency roster: agencies assign named workers to allocated shifts)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-1; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 Opening screen; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 Agent Chat

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User's typed request to assign named people to Shifts becomes a Proposal of kind WORKER_ASSIGNMENT with one item for each person on each Shift it names.
- **R2.** Iris finds each Release the request means among the Agency's ACCEPTED Releases on Shifts that have not ended, from the Unit, Position, date, and start time it gives.
- **R3.** When no Release or several match, or a person's first or last name is missing, Iris asks under [`REQ-AGENT-0003`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-agent-0003) and creates no Proposal until the User answers.
- **R4.** Each named person is matched to a Worker of the Agency under [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0002`](#req-workforce-0002).
- **R5.** A named person who matches no Worker of the Agency is proposed as a new Worker with the name given, and the item says a Worker will be created.
- **R6.** Each item shows the Worker and the Shift's Unit, Position, date, and times, and an item for a matched Worker is checked under [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003.R26`](#req-workforce-0003) when drafted and shows each reason it would be refused.
- **R7.** On apply, each accepted item creates its new Worker through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0001`](#req-workforce-0001) where one was proposed, then assigns the Worker through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003) with assigned_via ASSISTANT, under that requirement's checks.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-ASSISTANT-0003` Hand each typed request to the requirement that owns it](every-user.md#req-assistant-0003)

## Credentials

What a Shift requires of a Worker and how Iris confirms it.

<a id="req-compliance-0001"></a>

### Set Credential Types and where each is required

`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User defines Credential Types, such as a food handler card or a TB test, and where each is required. A requirement applies by org node, by Position, or by both.
- **Why:** Requirements vary by job, location and event *(WA-13: Certification requirements by region, position, unit and sector (e.g. alcohol service, food handler, TB tests))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-13; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance; [FAQ](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14WYK18DR1mu3SiXCUTRQw21Zjvzhl91U) Settings for each sector

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User adds or changes a Credential Type, and adds or removes a Credential Requirement.
- **R2.** A Credential Type has a unique name, a proof of ATTESTATION or VERIFIED_DOCUMENT, and a has_expiry flag; a duplicate name is refused.
- **R3.** A proof of ATTESTATION means an Agency Attestation satisfies the type, and VERIFIED_DOCUMENT means only a verified Credential document does.
- **R4.** A Credential Requirement names one active Credential Type, an org node or none, and a Position or none.
- **R5.** A requirement with an org node applies to every Unit at or under that node, and one with no org node applies to every Unit.
- **R6.** A requirement with a Position applies only to Shifts for that Position, and one with no Position applies to Shifts for every Position.
- **R7.** A second requirement with the same Credential Type, org node, and Position is refused.
- **R8.** A Credential Type is never deleted; setting is_active to false stops it being required and keeps its Credentials and Attestations, and it can be made active again.
- **R9.** Adding, changing, or removing a type or a requirement changes no stored Credential or Attestation and applies to every eligibility check made afterward, including for Workers already assigned.
- **R10.** Removing a Credential Requirement deletes it, with the removal kept in the Audit Trail, and the same requirement can be added again later.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-AGENCY-WEB-0007` Manage one Worker's Credentials and Attestations](agency-user.md#req-agency-web-0007)
- [`REQ-PROGRAM-WEB-0004` Manage Credential Types and Credential Requirements](program-user.md#req-program-web-0004)

<a id="req-compliance-0002"></a>

### Upload a Credential with its expiry

`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Agency User, Iris
- **What:** An Agency User uploads a Worker's Credential document with its type, issuer, number, and expiry date. Iris warns the Agency once before a verified Credential expires.
- **Why:**
  - Lapsed certifications shouldn't slip through *(WA-14: Certification upload with expiry tracking)*
  - Fraudulent certificates are a concern *(WA-15: AI document validation: checks expiry, issuer, signs of editing, and public registries where available)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-14; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-15; [FAQ](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14WYK18DR1mu3SiXCUTRQw21Zjvzhl91U) Every worker verified before the first shift; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User uploads a Credential only for a Worker of their own Agency and an active Credential Type, with the document file.
- **R2.** Issuer, number, and issued_on are optional, and expires_on is required when the Credential Type's has_expiry is true; a Credential missing it is not saved.
- **R3.** The CREDENTIALS upload type takes one PDF or image document for each Credential, and documents sent together are separate Uploads.
- **R4.** A document sent without details is a CREDENTIALS Upload: Iris reads the Worker's name, Credential Type, issuer, number, and dates from it into a one-item Proposal for the Agency User to confirm.
- **R5.** The Worker a document names is matched within the Agency by [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0002`](#req-workforce-0002); a document with no matching Worker is a problem and never creates a Worker.
- **R6.** A saved Credential starts as PENDING_CHECK with uploaded_by_id set and file_url naming the stored document, and is then checked by [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0003`](#req-compliance-0003).
- **R7.** A new Credential for a Worker and Credential Type that already has one sets replaces_id to the latest earlier one, which is kept unchanged.
- **R8.** After upload, an Agency User cannot change a Credential; a correction or a renewal is uploaded as a new Credential.
- **R9.** A daily job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001), at 08:00 in the program timezone, sends CREDENTIAL_EXPIRING for each VERIFIED Credential with no expiry_warned_at whose expires_on is today or at most CREDENTIAL_EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS days later.
- **R10.** CREDENTIAL_EXPIRING goes by email and in the app to every active Agency User of the Worker's Agency and sets expiry_warned_at, and is never sent for a Credential that a newer one replaces.
- **R11.** A Credential needs action when it is REJECTED, or VERIFIED with an expires_on already past or at most CREDENTIAL_EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS away, and no newer Credential of that Worker and Credential Type exists.
- **R12.** Today, for a Credential, is the current date in the program timezone that [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001) names.
- **R13.** A Credential entered on a form with its details stores its document through [`REQ-INTAKE-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-intake-0001) and creates no Upload and no Proposal.
- **R14.** Only an Agency User of the Worker's Agency and a Program User may open a Credential's document, which [`REQ-INTAKE-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-intake-0001) returns to them (C-35).
- **R15.** A CREDENTIAL_EXPIRING message names the Worker, the Credential Type, and the expires_on date.

**Screens that use it**

<a id="req-compliance-0003"></a>

### Validate Credential documents with AI and review what it cannot settle

`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0003` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris, Program User
- **What:** Iris checks each uploaded Credential document for expiry, issuer, and signs of editing, and with the issuer or a public registry where available. A Program User decides the ones the checks cannot settle.
- **Why:**
  - Fraudulent certificates are a concern *(WA-15: AI document validation: checks expiry, issuer, signs of editing, and public registries where available)*
  - Agencies attest; Compass audits *(WA-16: Attestation records and audit trail for agency-worker compliance (audited by Compass or the MSP))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-15; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-16; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance

**Rules**

- **R1.** An interval job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001) checks each PENDING_CHECK Credential for four things: the expiry date on the document, the issuer named on it, signs of editing, and the issuer or registry record.
- **R2.** The issuer or registry check is made through [`REQ-INTEGRATIONS-0006`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-integrations-0006); when its result is not available, that check is skipped and the result rests on the document checks.
- **R3.** The stored document file is passed to [`REQ-AGENT-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-agent-0001), which returns the issuer and dates it shows and whether it shows signs of editing, and code sets the status from them without a Proposal.
- **R4.** The result is REJECTED when the expiry date on the document is before today in the program timezone, or [`REQ-INTEGRATIONS-0006`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-integrations-0006) returns not confirmed.
- **R5.** The result is VERIFIED when it is not REJECTED, no sign of editing is found, the document's issuer and dates match the details uploaded, and every check that ran passed.
- **R6.** Any other outcome, including a document from which the model reads neither an issuer nor a date, is NEEDS_REVIEW.
- **R7.** Each result sets checked_at and a status_reason naming every check that failed or could not finish, and verification_reference when [`REQ-INTEGRATIONS-0006`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-integrations-0006) returned a reference.
- **R8.** A Program User decides each NEEDS_REVIEW Credential as VERIFIED or REJECTED with a review_note, which sets reviewed_by_id and reviewed_at.
- **R9.** VERIFIED and REJECTED are final: nobody changes the status of such a Credential.
- **R10.** When a Credential becomes VERIFIED or REJECTED, Iris sends CREDENTIAL_DECIDED in the app to the User who uploaded it, naming the Worker, the Credential Type, the status, and the status_reason or review_note.
- **R11.** The document matches when its issuer, issue date, and expiry date equal the uploaded issuer, issued_on, and expires_on; a detail left empty on upload is not compared, and issuers compare ignoring case and spacing.
- **R12.** A run in which [`REQ-AGENT-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-agent-0001) returns a failure leaves the Credential PENDING_CHECK and adds one to check_attempts, and the third such run makes it NEEDS_REVIEW.

<a id="req-compliance-0004"></a>

### Record Agency Attestations and keep their history

`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0004` · first slice

- **Who:** Agency User, Program User
- **What:** An Agency User attests that a Worker meets a Credential Type, such as work authorization. Iris keeps who attested, when, and to what, and never changes an Attestation.
- **Why:** Agencies attest; Compass audits *(WA-16: Attestation records and audit trail for agency-worker compliance (audited by Compass or the MSP))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-16; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User records an Attestation for a Worker of their own Agency and an active Credential Type, with a statement and an optional valid_until date.
- **R2.** Iris sets attested_by_id to that User and attested_at to the time the Attestation was recorded.
- **R3.** An Attestation is never edited or deleted; to change or renew one, the Agency User records a new Attestation.
- **R4.** For a Worker and Credential Type, only the Attestation with the latest attested_at counts, and it is current through its valid_until date, or without end when that is empty.
- **R5.** An Attestation can be recorded for any active Credential Type, but [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0005`](#req-compliance-0005) counts it only where the type's proof is ATTESTATION.
- **R6.** A Program User can see every Attestation, including replaced ones, with its Worker, Agency, Credential Type, statement, valid_until, attested_by_id, and attested_at.

<a id="req-compliance-0005"></a>

### Decide whether a Worker is eligible for a Shift

`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0005` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** A Worker is eligible for a Shift when every Credential Type the Shift requires is satisfied on its work date. Iris answers for a given Worker and Shift, with the reasons when the Worker is not eligible.
- **Why:**
  - Requirements vary by job, location and event *(WA-13: Certification requirements by region, position, unit and sector (e.g. alcohol service, food handler, TB tests))*
  - Lapsed certifications shouldn't slip through *(WA-14: Certification upload with expiry tracking)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-13; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-14; [FAQ](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14WYK18DR1mu3SiXCUTRQw21Zjvzhl91U) Every worker verified before the first shift; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance; [Demo app](https://github.com/Instawork/iris-demo/tree/feat/live-backend) lib/compliance.ts

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Shift requires every active Credential Type that has a Credential Requirement applying to the Shift's Unit and Position, as [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0001`](#req-compliance-0001) defines.
- **R2.** A required type is satisfied by a Credential of the Worker for that type that is VERIFIED and has no expires_on, or an expires_on on or after the Shift's work date.
- **R3.** A required type whose proof is ATTESTATION is also satisfied by the Worker's Attestation for it that is current on the work date, as [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0004`](#req-compliance-0004) defines.
- **R4.** A Credential that is PENDING_CHECK, NEEDS_REVIEW, or REJECTED never satisfies a type.
- **R5.** The Worker is eligible when every required type is satisfied, and always when the Shift requires none.
- **R6.** When the Worker is not eligible, the answer names each unsatisfied type and why: nothing on file, expired by the work date, still being checked, or rejected.
- **R7.** The answer is computed from the records at the moment it is asked, is not stored, and is the same whichever channel asks.
- **R8.** When [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0016`](#req-workforce-0016) asks again about a Worker already assigned to a Shift that has not started and the answer is not eligible, Iris sends WORKER_NOT_ELIGIBLE.
- **R9.** WORKER_NOT_ELIGIBLE goes by email and in the app to every active Agency User of the Worker's Agency and every active Unit User over the Shift's Unit, with the reasons.
- **R10.** This requirement never reads or changes Assignments; removing the Worker with NOT_ELIGIBLE is done by [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0016`](#req-workforce-0016).
- **R11.** A WORKER_NOT_ELIGIBLE message has the Worker as subject and names the Worker, the Shift's Unit, Position, date, and times, and each reason.

<a id="req-compliance-0006"></a>

### Request badge and system access at secured Units

`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0006`

- **Who:** Iris, Unit User
- **What:** At a Unit marked as a secured site, Iris raises one badge and system access request for each Worker at their first Assignment there. A Unit User marks it issued or revoked.
- **Why:** VMS requirement: manages badges and system access *(WA-17: Badge and system access requests for workers at secured sites)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-17

**Rules**

- **R1.** When a Worker is assigned to a Shift at a Unit whose is_secured_site is true and has no BadgeRequest for that Unit, Iris creates one as REQUESTED with requested_at set.
- **R2.** A Worker has at most one BadgeRequest for a Unit; a later Assignment there reuses it, and a REVOKED one becomes REQUESTED again with a new requested_at and its issued and revoked fields cleared.
- **R3.** A Unit User whose scope covers the Unit marks a REQUESTED BadgeRequest ISSUED, which sets issued_by_id and issued_at.
- **R4.** A Unit User whose scope covers the Unit marks a REQUESTED or ISSUED BadgeRequest REVOKED, which sets revoked_by_id and revoked_at.
- **R5.** A BadgeRequest in any status does not stop a Worker being assigned and is not part of eligibility.
- **R6.** Unit Users see the BadgeRequest status of each Worker assigned to Shifts at their secured Units.

## Labor rules

State and local rules, Work Weeks, and overtime.

<a id="req-labor-0001"></a>

### Hold state and local labor rules

`REQ-LABOR-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin
- **What:** Iris holds labor rules by state and city for meal and rest breaks, minimum wage, and overtime, so compliance does not depend on each Unit User. Instawork Admins load them as reference data. The pilot's rules come from Compass, as input I-10.
- **Why:** Rules vary by state and city; compliance shouldn't depend on the operator *(WA-18: State and local labor rules (breaks, minimum wage) applied at booking and on timesheets)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-18

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only an Instawork Admin adds, changes, or ends a Labor Rule.
- **R2.** Each rule has a two-letter state, an optional city, one kind, an effective_from date, and an optional effective_to date that is exclusive.
- **R3.** The kinds are MEAL_BREAK, REST_BREAK, MINIMUM_WAGE, DAILY_OVERTIME, WEEKLY_OVERTIME, and DAILY_DOUBLE_TIME.
- **R4.** A rule needs threshold_minutes for every kind except MINIMUM_WAGE, break_minutes for MEAL_BREAK and REST_BREAK, and minimum_wage for MINIMUM_WAGE; a rule missing its value is refused.
- **R5.** Two rules of the same state, city, and kind cannot cover the same date; the later one is refused until the earlier one is ended.
- **R6.** The rule in effect for a Unit, kind, and date has the Unit's state and covers the date; a rule whose city equals the Unit's city, compared as names are, wins over the statewide rule.
- **R7.** When no rule of a kind is in effect for a Unit and date, that kind does not apply there; Iris has no built-in default rules.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-ADMIN-WEB-0001` Instawork Admin home: reference data and the first Program User](instawork-admin.md#req-admin-web-0001)
- [`REQ-ADMIN-WEB-0004` Keep state and local Labor Rules](instawork-admin.md#req-admin-web-0004)

<a id="req-labor-0002"></a>

### Check break and minimum-wage rules at booking and on Timesheets

`REQ-LABOR-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Given a Unit, a work date, start and end times, break minutes, and a Pay Rate, Iris says which break and minimum-wage rules are not met. The checks flag and never block.
- **Why:** Rules vary by state and city; compliance shouldn't depend on the operator *(WA-18: State and local labor rules (breaks, minimum wage) applied at booking and on timesheets)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-18

**Rules**

- **R1.** A break is missed when the minutes from start to end, less the break minutes, are more than the MEAL_BREAK rule's threshold_minutes and the break minutes are fewer than its break_minutes.
- **R2.** The Pay Rate is below minimum wage when it is less than the MINIMUM_WAGE rule's minimum_wage in effect on the work date.
- **R3.** The caller gives the regular Pay Rate of the Agency's Rate Line; when there is no Rate Line, the minimum-wage check is not made.
- **R4.** REST_BREAK rules and a second meal break in one Shift are not checked in MVP, because Shifts and Timesheets record only one total of unpaid break minutes.
- **R5.** At booking, the check uses the Shift's scheduled start, end, and planned break, and a rule not met is shown as a flag that does not stop the booking.
- **R6.** On a Timesheet, the check uses the billed clock_in, clock_out, and break_minutes, and returns MISSED_BREAK or BELOW_MINIMUM_WAGE for [`REQ-TIME-0005`](#req-time-0005) to store.
- **R7.** Each check uses the Labor Rule in effect for the Unit on the work date, and passes when no rule of that kind is in effect.

<a id="req-labor-0003"></a>

### Track overtime within each Agency and alert

`REQ-LABOR-0003` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Iris adds up the minutes a Worker works for one Agency, across Units, in each Unit's Work Week, and alerts when an Assignment or Timesheet hours add overtime. Where OVERTIME_HARD_BLOCK is on, an Assignment that adds overtime is refused instead.
- **Why:** Flag overtime rather than block it; some locations want a hard block, festivals accept overtime *(WA-19: Overtime tracking and alerts within each agency, with an optional hard block per location)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-19

**Rules**

- **R1.** Overtime is tracked for one Worker of one Agency across every Unit, never across Agencies, in each distinct Work Week holding the changed work date at a Unit of the Worker's counted Shifts.
- **R2.** The caller gives the Worker's counted Shifts with work dates within six days of the changed work date, each with its Unit, work date, start time, and minutes, both before and after the change.
- **R3.** When Timesheet hours are saved, [`REQ-TIME-0001`](#req-time-0001) counts a Shift at its Timesheets' worked_minutes once hours are entered, and otherwise at its scheduled minutes less the planned break.
- **R4.** When a Worker is assigned, [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003) counts every Shift at its scheduled minutes less the planned break, because it cannot read Timesheets.
- **R5.** A change adds overtime at a Unit when the overtime plus double-time minutes of the Shifts at that Unit, classified as in [`REQ-LABOR-0005`](#req-labor-0005) within that Unit's Work Week, are greater after the change than before.
- **R6.** When an Assignment would add overtime at a Unit and OVERTIME_HARD_BLOCK is true for that Unit or for the Unit of the Shift being assigned, the answer is to refuse it and send no alert.
- **R7.** In every other case a change that adds overtime is allowed, and Iris sends one OVERTIME_ALERT for each Unit where it adds overtime; Timesheet hours are never refused for overtime.
- **R8.** Each OVERTIME_ALERT goes in the app to every active Agency User of the Worker's Agency and every active Unit User over that Unit or over the changed Shift's Unit.
- **R9.** An OVERTIME_ALERT names the Worker, the Unit, its Work Week, and the overtime plus double-time minutes of the Worker's Shifts at that Unit in that week after the change.

<a id="req-labor-0004"></a>

### Use each Unit's own Work Week for overtime and reporting

`REQ-LABOR-0004` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Each Unit has its own Work Week, starting on the weekday stored as its work_week_start. A Program User sets that day when adding or editing the Unit.
- **Why:** 39 pay areas; work weeks start on nearly every day *(WA-20: Per-unit work week configuration for overtime and reporting)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-20

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit's Work Week is seven dates in a row that begin on its work_week_start weekday, with dates taken in the Unit's timezone.
- **R2.** A work date belongs to the Work Week that begins on the latest work_week_start weekday on or before it.
- **R3.** A Shift and its Timesheets belong to the Work Week of the Shift's work date, even when the Shift ends on a later date.
- **R4.** Overtime tracking, the classification of minutes, and weekly reporting for a Unit all use this Work Week.
- **R5.** The Work Week for any date is worked out from the work_week_start stored on the Unit at the time it is asked for.

Example, with overtime after 40 hours a week: Unit A's week starts Monday and Unit B's Thursday. Ten hours a day Monday to Wednesday at A and Thursday to Saturday at B bill no overtime; the same days with the Units swapped bill 20 hours of it. Needs HR, legal, and payroll.
- [D-201](open-questions.md#d-201) In what order are a Worker's minutes classified?
- [D-203](open-questions.md#d-203) Which start day applies to past weeks after a Unit's Work Week start changes?

<a id="req-labor-0005"></a>

### Classify minutes as regular, overtime, or double time

`REQ-LABOR-0005` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Given the Timesheets one Worker has in one Work Week, across Units, Iris splits each Timesheet's worked minutes into regular, overtime, and double time under the Labor Rules in effect. It only calculates; [`REQ-TIME-0001`](#req-time-0001) saves the result.
- **Why:**
  - Flag overtime rather than block it; some locations want a hard block, festivals accept overtime *(WA-19: Overtime tracking and alerts within each agency, with an optional hard block per location)*
  - 39 pay areas; work weeks start on nearly every day *(WA-20: Per-unit work week configuration for overtime and reporting)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-19; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-20; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §3 Supplier Rates

**Rules**

- **R1.** Classification covers one Worker's Timesheets, at every Unit, whose work dates fall in one Work Week of one Unit; the caller gives each one's Unit, work date, clock_in, worked_minutes, and, if locked, stored classes.
- **R2.** Timesheets are taken in order of clock_in, and all of a Timesheet's minutes count on its Shift's work date, even past midnight.
- **R3.** On one work date, counting across Units, minutes past the DAILY_DOUBLE_TIME threshold_minutes are double time, and other minutes past the DAILY_OVERTIME threshold_minutes are overtime.
- **R4.** Minutes the daily rules leave regular count toward the WEEKLY_OVERTIME threshold_minutes, locked Timesheets' stored regular minutes first and then the others in clock_in order, and those past it are overtime.
- **R5.** Every remaining minute is regular, so each Timesheet's three classes add up to its worked_minutes.
- **R6.** Each threshold comes from the Labor Rule in effect for the Timesheet's own Unit on its work date, and a kind with no rule in effect there is not applied.
- **R7.** The caller classifies a Timesheet within the Work Week of that Timesheet's own Unit; [`REQ-TIME-0001`](#req-time-0001) saves the result only to Timesheets that are not locked, and a locked Timesheet keeps its stored classes.
- **R8.** [`REQ-LABOR-0003`](#req-labor-0003) uses the same steps on scheduled Shifts, with the scheduled start as clock_in and the scheduled minutes less the planned break as worked_minutes.

Ten hours a day Monday to Wednesday at A and Thursday to Saturday at B bill no overtime; the same days with the Units swapped bill 20 hours of it. Needs HR, legal, and payroll.

## Timesheets

Hours worked: intake, approval, corrections, and lock.

<a id="req-time-0001"></a>

### Hold a Timesheet for each assigned Worker

`REQ-TIME-0001`

- **Who:** Iris, Agency User
- **What:** Iris creates a Draft Timesheet for each assigned Worker when the Shift ends. It holds the hours the Agency bills, the Bill Rates, and the minutes in each hour class.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) 4.3; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shifts; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shift statuses; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) Data Model

**Rules**

- **R1.** An interval job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001) creates one DRAFT Timesheet for each ASSIGNED Assignment that has none, on every Shift that is not CANCELLED and whose ends_at has passed.
- **R2.** A new Timesheet takes the Shift's Position and Department and the Release's regular, overtime, and double-time Bill Rates, with no clock times, no break, and is_no_show false.
- **R3.** An Assignment has one Timesheet, or one for each part once it is split under [`REQ-TIME-0008`](#req-time-0008).
- **R4.** An Agency User of the Worker's Agency enters or changes clock_in, clock_out, and break_minutes while the Timesheet is DRAFT or REJECTED, and in no other status.
- **R5.** A change is refused when clock_out is not later than clock_in, or when break_minutes is negative or not less than the minutes between them; an empty value is not checked.
- **R6.** Clock times are kept to the whole minute, with seconds dropped.
- **R7.** worked_minutes is clock_out minus clock_in minus break_minutes, and is 0 while either clock time is empty or is_no_show is true.
- **R8.** Whenever worked_minutes changes, Iris reclassifies through [`REQ-LABOR-0005`](#req-labor-0005) every Timesheet of that Worker whose own Unit's Work Week holds the changed work date, and saves the three minute classes on those not locked.
- **R9.** After that, Iris gives [`REQ-LABOR-0003`](#req-labor-0003) the Worker's Shifts with work dates within six days of the changed one, before and after the change, and it alerts for each Unit where the change adds overtime.
- **R10.** Nobody enters or changes a Bill Rate on a Timesheet: its three rates stay those of R2, or of the Rate Line for a part [`REQ-TIME-0008`](#req-time-0008) splits to another Position.
- **R11.** A Timesheet's amount for each hour class is computed from its Bill Rate and minutes whenever it is asked for, and is never stored on the Timesheet.
- **R12.** Every change to a Timesheet is written to the Audit Trail with who made it, when, and the old and new values.
- **R13.** When [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003) assigns a Worker after the Shift's ends_at, this requirement creates that Assignment's DRAFT Timesheet in the same transaction, so hours can be saved to it at once.
- **R14.** A clock time is a local date and time at the Unit; one that does not exist on a daylight-saving change is refused, and one that occurs twice means the occurrence nearest the scheduled time.
- **R15.** Each new Timesheet and each change to a Timesheet's hours or no-show is published as an event; [`REQ-TIPS-0004`](#req-tips-0004) re-splits its Tip Pools, and [`REQ-TIME-0005`](#req-time-0005) rechecks it as [`REQ-TIME-0005.R1`](#req-time-0005) says.

<a id="req-time-0002"></a>

### Submit and approve Timesheets daily or per Event

`REQ-TIME-0002`

- **Who:** Agency User, Unit User
- **What:** An Agency User submits Timesheets as soon as a Shift ends, and a Unit User approves them the same day or per Event. Nothing waits for the end of the week.
- **Why:** The true cost of a Monday event shouldn't stay hidden until week end *(TS-8: Daily or per-event timesheet submission and approval, not just at week end)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-8; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Timesheets, Tips & Expenses

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User submits a DRAFT or REJECTED Timesheet of their own Agency's Worker, which makes it SUBMITTED and sets submitted_by_id and submitted_at.
- **R2.** Submitting is not refused for a missing clock time; [`REQ-TIME-0005`](#req-time-0005) checks every submission and lists such a Timesheet with MISSING_TIMES.
- **R3.** Submitting a REJECTED Timesheet clears its rejected_reason.
- **R4.** An Agency User can submit one Timesheet, or in one step every DRAFT and REJECTED Timesheet of their Agency for one Shift, one Event, or one work date at a Unit.
- **R5.** A Unit User whose scope covers the Shift's Unit approves a SUBMITTED Timesheet, which makes it APPROVED and sets approved_by_id and approved_at.
- **R6.** Approval is refused while exception_reasons include MISSING_TIMES or PENDING_EXPENSE; the Unit User first corrects the hours or decides the Expense.
- **R7.** A Unit User can approve one Timesheet, or in one step every SUBMITTED Timesheet in their scope for one Shift, one Event, or one work date at a Unit.
- **R8.** In a bulk step, Timesheets that cannot be submitted or approved are left as they are and listed with the reason.
- **R9.** A Timesheet can be submitted and approved as soon as it exists; neither step waits for the Work Week or any other period to end.

<a id="req-time-0003"></a>

### Read Timesheets in any format and match them to Shifts

`REQ-TIME-0003`

- **Who:** Agency User, Unit User
- **What:** A user sends hours as a template, PDF, CSV, spreadsheet, or photo of a paper sign-in sheet. Iris matches each line to a Worker's Timesheet and proposes the hours for approval.
- **Why:** Most temp time is on paper today; only about 2% runs through MyStaff *(TS-5: Timesheet intake in any format (PDF, CSV, image), matched to shifts automatically)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-5; [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) OCR to match paper timesheets; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Timesheets, Tips & Expenses; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Uploads; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Templates

**Rules**

- **R1.** The TIMESHEETS upload type takes the template or a PDF, CSV, spreadsheet, or image in any layout, including a photo of a paper sign-in sheet read with OCR.
- **R2.** An Agency User uploads hours for their own Agency's Workers, and a Unit User for Shifts at Units in their scope.
- **R3.** A line's Shift is the one with its shift_id, or else the single Shift at the named Unit on that work date for that Position.
- **R4.** A line's Worker is matched by [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0002`](#req-workforce-0002) within the Agency for an Agency User's file, and among the Workers assigned to the Shift for a Unit User's file.
- **R5.** A matched line points to the Timesheet of that Worker's Assignment on that Shift; a line with no single Shift, Worker, or unsplit Timesheet is a problem.
- **R6.** Every line appears in a Proposal with the hours read, and the uploader matches problem lines by hand, edits them, or drops them before anything is saved.
- **R7.** A clock time given without a date is read as the occurrence of that time nearest the Shift's scheduled start, for clock_in, or end, for clock_out.
- **R8.** When an Agency User's line names a Worker with no Assignment on the Shift, the Proposal offers to assign them through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003), creating a new Worker through [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0001`](#req-workforce-0001) if needed.
- **R9.** An Agency User's accepted lines save clock_in, clock_out, and break_minutes to DRAFT and REJECTED Timesheets through [`REQ-TIME-0001`](#req-time-0001), which checks them and recomputes worked_minutes and the hour classes.
- **R10.** A Unit User's accepted lines are saved as corrections to SUBMITTED and APPROVED Timesheets under [`REQ-TIME-0006`](#req-time-0006), each with the reason in its reason column.
- **R11.** A line for a Timesheet the uploader may not change in its current status is reported as a problem and not saved.
- **R12.** A line whose no_show column is Yes marks the Timesheet a no-show under [`REQ-TIME-0009`](#req-time-0009) instead of saving clock times.
- **R13.** An upload never submits or approves a Timesheet; those stay separate steps in [`REQ-TIME-0002`](#req-time-0002).
- **R14.** A line whose no_show column is not Yes needs both clock_in and clock_out; a line missing either is a problem for the uploader to complete or drop.
- **R15.** A second line for the same Timesheet in one file is a duplicate of the first.
- **R16.** A Unit User's line with an empty reason is a problem for the uploader to complete or drop, because [`REQ-TIME-0006`](#req-time-0006) and [`REQ-TIME-0009`](#req-time-0009) take a Unit User's change only with a reason.

<a id="req-time-0004"></a>

### Edit Timesheets in plain language

`REQ-TIME-0004`

- **Who:** Agency User, Unit User
- **What:** A user describes a Timesheet change in the assistant, such as “Grace moved to bartender at 3:45”. Iris proposes the exact edits, and saves only those the user approves.
- **Why:** Fast handling of edge cases *(TS-6: Natural-language timesheet edits ("Grace moved to bartender at 3:45"))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-6; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Timesheets, Tips & Expenses; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 Agent Chat

**Rules**

- **R1.** Iris turns the request into a Proposal of kind TIMESHEET_EDITS that lists each Timesheet with the field, its current value, and the new value.
- **R2.** Iris proposes only changes the user could make by hand in the Timesheet's current status, and explains any it leaves out.
- **R3.** When a name or a Shift in the request fits more than one Timesheet, Iris asks which one before proposing anything.
- **R4.** A change of Position or Department partway through a Shift is proposed as a split at the stated time, saved through [`REQ-TIME-0008`](#req-time-0008).
- **R5.** Accepted items are saved through the requirement that owns each change: [`REQ-TIME-0001`](#req-time-0001) or [`REQ-TIME-0006`](#req-time-0006) for hours, [`REQ-TIME-0008`](#req-time-0008) for a split, and [`REQ-TIME-0009`](#req-time-0009) for a no-show.
- **R6.** A Unit User can ask to approve the Timesheets of a period; the TIMESHEET_EDITS Proposal lists each SUBMITTED one with its exception_reasons, and accepted ones are approved through [`REQ-TIME-0002`](#req-time-0002).
- **R7.** An Agency User can ask to submit their DRAFT and REJECTED Timesheets for a period, also as a TIMESHEET_EDITS Proposal, and accepted ones are submitted through [`REQ-TIME-0002`](#req-time-0002).

<a id="req-time-0005"></a>

### Auto-approve within tolerance and surface exceptions

`REQ-TIME-0005`

- **Who:** Iris, Unit User
- **What:** Iris approves a submitted Timesheet whose billed times match the schedule within the Approval Tolerance and that has no other exception. Every other one goes to the Unit's exception list with its reasons.
- **Why:**
  - Approvals take too long; operators would comply if it took minutes *(TS-7: Exception-based approval: auto-approve within schedule tolerance, surface the rest on a dashboard)*
  - Units need to see deviations and push back on vendors *(RC-10: Rate variance flags at booking and on approved timesheets, with drill-down (e.g. card $25, paid $29, and why))*
  - Rules vary by state and city; compliance shouldn't depend on the operator *(WA-18: State and local labor rules (breaks, minimum wage) applied at booking and on timesheets)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-7; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-10; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-18

**Rules**

- **R1.** Iris checks a Timesheet each time it becomes SUBMITTED, and again whenever its hours, no-show, or Expenses change while it is SUBMITTED, or while it is APPROVED and not locked, as R12 says.
- **R2.** Each check replaces exception_reasons with every reason that applies; when none applies, the Timesheet becomes APPROVED with approved_at set and approved_by_id left empty.
- **R3.** MISSING_TIMES applies when is_no_show is false and clock_in or clock_out is empty.
- **R4.** OUTSIDE_TOLERANCE applies when clock_in differs from the Shift's starts_at, or clock_out from its ends_at, by more than APPROVAL_TOLERANCE_MINUTES minutes, resolved for the Shift's Unit.
- **R5.** MISSED_BREAK and BELOW_MINIMUM_WAGE apply when [`REQ-LABOR-0002`](#req-labor-0002) returns them for the billed times, the break, and the regular Pay Rate of the Timesheet's Rate Line.
- **R6.** The Timesheet's Rate Line is its Release's rate_line_id, or for a part split to another Position, the line [`REQ-RATES-0005`](#req-rates-0005) finds for that Position.
- **R7.** A Timesheet that bills its Release's Bill Rates never carries RATE_VARIANCE; only a part split to another Position can, as R13 says.
- **R8.** PENDING_EXPENSE applies when any Expense on the Timesheet is PENDING.
- **R9.** Overtime or double-time minutes alone add no reason, and a no-show Timesheet can carry only PENDING_EXPENSE.
- **R10.** For a split Timesheet, the first part's clock_in, the last part's clock_out, and the parts' total break are compared with the schedule, the planned break, and the break rule, and every part carries the result.
- **R11.** A SUBMITTED Timesheet with any reason stays SUBMITTED and appears, with its reasons, on the exception list of each Unit User whose scope covers the Shift's Unit.
- **R12.** exception_reasons are kept after approval, and a check of an APPROVED Timesheet replaces them without changing its status, approved_by_id, or approved_at.
- **R13.** For a part split to another Position, RATE_VARIANCE applies instead when [`REQ-RATES-0006`](#req-rates-0006) reports a rate variance, or no contracted rate, for that Position's regular Bill Rate.
- **R14.** Each Timesheet also shows the rate variance [`REQ-RATES-0006`](#req-rates-0006) finds between its three Bill Rates and the contracted Rate Line, before and after approval; that flag alone adds no reason.
- **R15.** AGENCY_TIP applies when the Timesheet has a tip with no pool and no cashier PIN, which only an Agency User enters.
- **R16.** Agency Users see the exception_reasons on the Timesheets of their own Agency's Workers.
- **R17.** LATE_SUBMISSION applies when submitted_at is later than LOCK_WINDOW_HOURS hours, resolved for the Shift's Unit, after the Shift's ends_at.
- **R18.** ADDED_AFTER_SHIFT applies when the Timesheet's Assignment has an assigned_at later than the Shift's ends_at, which [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0003`](#req-workforce-0003) allows even beyond the Release's headcount.
- **R19.** SHORT_BREAK applies when is_no_show is false, both clock times are set, and break_minutes, counting empty as 0, are fewer than the Shift's planned break_minutes.
- **R20.** MIXED_WORK_WEEKS applies when the Worker has another Timesheet, not a no-show, with a work date fewer than seven days from this one's, at a Unit whose work_week_start differs from this Unit's.

<a id="req-time-0006"></a>

### Correct or reject a Timesheet with a reason

`REQ-TIME-0006`

- **Who:** Unit User, Iris
- **What:** A Unit User corrects the hours on a submitted or approved Timesheet, or rejects a submitted one back to the Agency, always with a reason. Each change to hours notifies the other party.
- **Why:** Approvals take too long; operators would comply if it took minutes *(TS-7: Exception-based approval: auto-approve within schedule tolerance, surface the rest on a dashboard)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-7; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 How hour changes work; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shifts; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Timesheets, Tips & Expenses

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User whose scope covers the Shift's Unit can correct clock_in, clock_out, and break_minutes on a SUBMITTED or APPROVED Timesheet that is not locked, and must give a reason.
- **R2.** A correction is saved through [`REQ-TIME-0001`](#req-time-0001), which applies the same checks as to hours an Agency enters and recomputes worked_minutes and the hour classes; values it refuses are not saved.
- **R3.** A correction replaces the billed values; the old values, the new values, who made it, and the reason stay in the Audit Trail, where both parties can see them.
- **R4.** A corrected APPROVED Timesheet stays APPROVED, and a corrected SUBMITTED Timesheet is checked again by [`REQ-TIME-0005`](#req-time-0005).
- **R5.** For a Timesheet with OUTSIDE_TOLERANCE, the Unit User can apply the Shift's scheduled start and end as the correction in one step, still with a reason.
- **R6.** A Unit User can reject a SUBMITTED Timesheet with a required reason, which makes it REJECTED and sets rejected_reason; an APPROVED Timesheet cannot be rejected.
- **R7.** On a rejection, Iris sends TIMESHEET_REJECTED with the reason, by email and in the app, to every active Agency User of the Worker's Agency.
- **R8.** Iris sends TIMESHEET_CHANGED to the other party when hours, breaks, or no-show change on a Timesheet submitted at least once, and whenever a Unit User sets or clears a no-show.
- **R9.** For a Unit User's change the other party is every active Agency User of the Worker's Agency; for an Agency User's change it is every active Unit User whose scope covers the Unit.

<a id="req-time-0007"></a>

### Lock approved Timesheets after the Lock Window

`REQ-TIME-0007`

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** An approved Timesheet locks once the Lock Window after its Shift has passed, 48 hours by default, and never sooner than 24 hours after its approval. A locked Timesheet cannot change, and an unapproved one stays open and shows as late. Each Timesheet locks on its own time, whatever Tip Pool covers it.
- **Why:** Edits allowed for up to about 3 weeks make reporting stale *(TS-9: Configurable timesheet lock window (e.g. 24–48 hours after an event))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-9

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Timesheet's lock time is the later of its Shift's ends_at plus LOCK_WINDOW_HOURS hours, resolved for the Shift's Unit, and its approved_at plus 24 hours.
- **R2.** An interval job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-jobs-0001) sets locked_at on each APPROVED Timesheet whose lock time has passed.
- **R3.** A Timesheet that is DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or REJECTED when the window closes does not lock; it stays open and shows as late to its Agency and its Unit until it is approved.
- **R4.** Once locked_at is set, nobody can change the Timesheet's hours, no-show, Bill Rates, tips, Expenses, or status, or split it, and its minutes are never reclassified.
- **R5.** Nothing unlocks a Timesheet in MVP, including a later change to LOCK_WINDOW_HOURS; corrections after lock arrive with invoicing in Phase 2.
- **R7.** Each Timesheet locks at its own lock time, whatever Tip Pool covers it, and from then [`REQ-TIPS-0001.R17`](#req-tips-0001) keeps its tips as they are.
- **R8.** Each lock is published as an event, to which [`REQ-TIPS-0004`](#req-tips-0004) reacts under its own rules.

<a id="req-time-0008"></a>

### Split a Timesheet when a Worker changes role

`REQ-TIME-0008`

- **Who:** Agency User, Unit User
- **What:** When a Worker moves to another Position or Department partway through a Shift, the Timesheet splits at that time. Each part keeps its own Position, Department, and Bill Rates.
- **Why:** Mid-shift role and rate changes are rarely captured *(TS-10: Split a shift by time and position for mid-shift role changes (e.g. bartender → barback))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-10; [Demo feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AQi9DSbYzvEEijmSjCUajHHymowKWYXTPcO3hDEkWc/edit) split can also be department driven; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Timesheets, Tips & Expenses

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User splits a DRAFT or REJECTED Timesheet, and a Unit User, with a reason, a SUBMITTED or APPROVED one that is not locked.
- **R2.** The user gives a switch time after clock_in and before clock_out, and a new Position, a new Department of the Shift's Unit, or both; anything else is refused.
- **R3.** The Timesheet keeps the time before the switch, and a new Timesheet on the same Assignment, with split_from_id set, takes the time from the switch on.
- **R4.** The new part copies the status, submission and approval details, rejected_reason, and exception_reasons of the Timesheet it came from, and its is_no_show is false.
- **R5.** break_minutes stay on the first part unless the user moves some to the new part, and the two parts' break_minutes always add up to the original.
- **R6.** A part whose Position changed takes the three Bill Rates of the Rate Line [`REQ-RATES-0005`](#req-rates-0005) finds for the Agency, that Position, the Unit, and the work date; any other part keeps the original rates.
- **R7.** When no Rate Line exists for the new Position, the part keeps the original Bill Rates and carries RATE_VARIANCE whenever it is checked.
- **R8.** Each part is charged to its own Department's cost center.
- **R9.** A part can be split again in the same way.
- **R10.** A split of a Timesheet that has been submitted counts as a change to its hours, so [`REQ-TIME-0006`](#req-time-0006) notifies the other party.
- **R11.** Both parts are saved through [`REQ-TIME-0001`](#req-time-0001), which checks each part's times and recomputes its worked_minutes and hour classes.

<a id="req-time-0009"></a>

### Mark a Worker as a no-show

`REQ-TIME-0009`

- **Who:** Agency User, Unit User
- **What:** An Agency User or a Unit User marks an assigned Worker as a no-show on the Timesheet. Its minutes become zero, so no hours are charged for that Worker. A Unit User can mark one before the Agency submits.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shifts; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §5 Invoices

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User marks a no-show on a DRAFT or REJECTED Timesheet, and a Unit User, with a reason, on any Timesheet that is not locked, including a DRAFT one.
- **R2.** Marking sets is_no_show to true and no_show_by to the acting role, and clears clock_in, clock_out, and break_minutes through [`REQ-TIME-0001`](#req-time-0001), so worked_minutes and every hour class become 0.
- **R3.** An Agency User clears a mark only if an Agency User set it and the Timesheet is DRAFT or REJECTED; a Unit User clears any mark, with a reason, until the Timesheet locks.
- **R4.** A no-show Timesheet has no hours amount and counts no tips, so only an approved Expense on it adds to spend.
- **R5.** Setting or clearing the mark notifies the other party through [`REQ-TIME-0006`](#req-time-0006): always when a Unit User does it, and otherwise once the Timesheet has been submitted.
- **R6.** The mark opens no Worker issue; a Unit User reports a no-show as a Worker issue of category NO_SHOW in a separate step.
- **R7.** Clearing sets is_no_show to false and empties no_show_by, after which hours are entered again.
- **R8.** While is_no_show is true, a change to clock_in, clock_out, or break_minutes is refused until the mark is cleared.
