## Tips and expenses

Money passed through at cost alongside hours.

<a id="req-tips-0001"></a>

### Hold each Timesheet's tips and take the tips an Agency enters

`REQ-TIPS-0001`

- **Who:** Agency User, Iris
- **What:** Every tip is an allocation on one Timesheet and passes through at cost. An Agency User enters a Worker's own tip on the Timesheet, in the app or by chat. No tip changes once its Timesheet locks.
- **Why:** Tip pooling is manual; stadiums use cashier PINs *(TS-11: Tips entry (bulk or chat), split by hours worked)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-11; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shifts; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §5 Invoices; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Timesheets, Tips & Expenses

**Rules**

- **R14.** An Agency User enters, changes, or removes a tip for a Worker of their own Agency on a DRAFT or REJECTED Timesheet, as a TipAllocation with no pool and no PIN.
- **R15.** A Timesheet's tips are the sum of its TipAllocations, counted as zero while it is a no-show, and pass through at that amount with no markup.
- **R17.** No TipAllocation is added to, changed on, or removed from a locked Timesheet, and any action that would do so is refused.
- **R18.** A typed tip that repeats a tip an Agency User already saved on the same Timesheet for the same amount is a duplicate, whose suggested fix is to reject it.
- **R19.** An Agency User can also ask the assistant to enter a Worker's tip; the TIP_ENTRY Proposal lists each Timesheet and amount, and accepted items are saved under R14.
- **R20.** This requirement registers the TIP_ENTRY save step, which saves an Agency User's tip under R14 and hands a Tip Pool item to [`REQ-TIPS-0004`](#req-tips-0004) once that requirement registers for it.

<a id="req-tips-0002"></a>

### Add and approve expenses

`REQ-TIPS-0002`

- **Who:** Agency User, Unit User
- **What:** An Agency User adds expenses the Agency paid for a Worker on a Shift, such as parking or a required background check. A Unit User approves or rejects each one, and approved expenses pass through at cost.
- **Why:** Expenses flow through the same process *(TS-12: Expense entry and approval)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-12; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Timesheets, Tips & Expenses

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Agency User adds an Expense to a DRAFT or REJECTED Timesheet of a Worker of their own Agency.
- **R2.** An Expense has a kind of PARKING, BACKGROUND_CHECK, or OTHER, an amount above zero, and a note, which is required when the kind is OTHER.
- **R3.** An Expense is added one at a time in the app, from an EXPENSES file, or in the assistant as a Proposal of kind EXPENSE_ENTRY.
- **R4.** An EXPENSES row's Shift is the one with its shift_id, or else the single Shift at the named Unit on that date for that Position; [`REQ-WORKFORCE-0002`](#req-workforce-0002) matches its Worker within the uploader's Agency.
- **R5.** A new Expense is PENDING with added_by_id set, and the Agency User can change or delete it while it is PENDING and its Timesheet is DRAFT or REJECTED.
- **R6.** A Unit User whose scope covers the Shift's Unit approves or rejects each PENDING Expense on a SUBMITTED Timesheet, which sets decided_by_id and decided_at.
- **R7.** A rejection needs a reason, saved as rejected_reason, and an APPROVED or REJECTED Expense is never changed.
- **R8.** An APPROVED Expense passes through at its amount with no markup, and a REJECTED one adds nothing.
- **R9.** A matched row points to the Timesheet of that Worker's Assignment on that Shift, or to its first part if split; a row with no single Shift, Worker, or Timesheet is a problem.
- **R10.** An Agency User can ask the assistant to add one Expense to several Workers of a Shift; the EXPENSE_ENTRY Proposal lists one item for each Timesheet with the Worker, kind, amount, and note.
- **R11.** A request for everyone who worked a Shift covers each DRAFT or REJECTED Timesheet of the Agency's Workers on it that is not a no-show; Timesheets in another status are left out and named.
- **R12.** When the request does not fit exactly one Shift, or names a Worker who fits several Timesheets, Iris asks which before proposing anything, as [`REQ-AGENT-0003`](behind-the-scenes.md#req-agent-0003) requires.
- **R13.** Each accepted item is saved as a PENDING Expense under the same rules as one added in the app.
- **R14.** An EXPENSES row or typed Expense that repeats a saved Expense or an earlier row in Timesheet, kind, and amount is a duplicate, whose suggested fix is to reject it.
- **R15.** Deciding an Expense publishes the change, and [`REQ-TIME-0005`](#req-time-0005) then checks its SUBMITTED Timesheet again, as [`REQ-TIME-0005.R1`](#req-time-0005) requires; this requirement changes no Timesheet.

<a id="req-tips-0003"></a>

### Apply tip tax rules by state once Compass names them

`REQ-TIPS-0003`

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Iris will apply each state's tip tax rules, such as New York's, to tips. Sheet feature TS-13 is not delivered: no rule is applied until Compass names the rules under D-15 and supplies them as input I-11.
- **Why:** Rules vary (e.g. New York) *(TS-13: Tip tax rules by state)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-13

**Rules**

- **R1.** Until Compass names the tip tax rules, Iris applies none, and tips pass through at the amounts entered.
- **R2.** This requirement adds no behavior, and TS-13 counts as not delivered, until D-15 is answered and input I-11 arrives; it is not approved or built before then.

<a id="req-tips-0004"></a>

### Split Tip Pools by hours and credit cashier PIN tips

`REQ-TIPS-0004`

- **Who:** Unit User, Iris
- **What:** A Unit User enters a Tip Pool for a Unit and date, or one Shift or Event on it, and Iris splits it across Workers by minutes worked. Scheduled minutes count until a Worker's hours are entered, and a share is fixed once its Timesheet locks. A tip entered under a cashier PIN goes whole to the Worker that PIN is mapped to.
- **Why:** Tip pooling is manual; stadiums use cashier PINs *(TS-11: Tips entry (bulk or chat), split by hours worked)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-11; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) 4.4; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Timesheets, Tips & Expenses

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User enters a Tip Pool for a Unit in their scope and a work date, with an amount above zero, optionally narrowed to one Shift or to one Event, never both.
- **R2.** A pool is entered in the app, from a TIPS file, or in the assistant as a TIP_ENTRY Proposal with one item per pool, whose summary lists each Worker's share before anything is saved.
- **R3.** A pool covers every Timesheet on a Shift at that Unit on that work date, narrowed to its Shift or Event when set, whatever the Agency or the Timesheet's status.
- **R4.** A pool's open amount is its amount less its shares on locked Timesheets, each of which keeps the share it held when it locked.
- **R5.** Each covered Timesheet that is not locked and has counted minutes (R7) gets a share: the open amount times those minutes divided by the counted minutes of all such Timesheets, rounded down to the cent.
- **R6.** Cents left over go one each to the shares with the largest dropped fractions, ties to the lowest Timesheet id, so the shares add up to the open amount exactly.
- **R7.** A covered Timesheet's counted minutes are its worked_minutes once both clock times are entered, its Shift's scheduled minutes less the planned break until then, and 0 while it is a no-show.
- **R8.** Each share is a TipAllocation with tip_pool_id set.
- **R9.** While no covered Timesheet that is not locked has counted minutes, the open amount is unallocated: it stays on the pool, is credited to no Timesheet, and adds nothing to spend.
- **R10.** Iris splits the open amount when the pool is entered or changed, and whenever [`REQ-TIME-0001.R15`](#req-time-0001) publishes that a covered Timesheet was created or that its hours or no-show changed.
- **R11.** When a Timesheet's change leaves unallocated an open amount that was shared before it, Iris sends TIP_NOT_CREDITED to every active Unit User whose scope covers the pool's Unit, naming the pool and the amount.
- **R12.** A Unit User can change or delete a Tip Pool or a PIN tip of a Unit in their scope.
- **R13.** Entering, changing, or deleting a Tip Pool is refused when a Timesheet it covers, would cover, or holds a share on is locked, and so is a PIN tip whose Timesheet is locked.
- **R14.** A Unit User maps a cashier PIN at a Unit in their scope to one Worker from valid_from until an optional valid_to.
- **R15.** A mapping is refused when the same PIN at that Unit is already mapped on any of its dates.
- **R16.** A Unit User may set or change the valid_to of a cashier PIN mapping in their scope, and its PIN, Worker, and valid_from never change.
- **R17.** A Unit User enters a cashier PIN tip at a Unit in their scope, creating one TipAllocation, with cashier_pin_id set, for the whole amount on the Timesheet of that PIN's Worker there on that date.
- **R18.** When that Worker has several Timesheets there on that date, the tip goes to the one on the earliest Shift among those neither a no-show nor locked, and to its first part if split.
- **R19.** A PIN tip is refused when no CashierPin is valid for that PIN, Unit, and date, or its Worker has no Timesheet there on that date that is neither a no-show nor locked.
- **R20.** When a Timesheet that holds a PIN tip becomes a no-show, the tip stays on it and counts as zero, and Iris sends TIP_NOT_CREDITED to the Unit Users R11 names.
- **R21.** In a TIPS file, a row with a cashier PIN is a PIN tip and every other row is a Tip Pool.
- **R22.** A TIPS row or typed pool that repeats a saved one or an earlier row in Unit, work date, Shift, Event, PIN, and amount is a duplicate, whose suggested fix is to reject it.
- **R23.** When [`REQ-ORDERING-0011`](#req-ordering-0011) attaches a Shift to an Event, moves it to another, or detaches it, Iris splits again the open amount of every pool narrowed to either Event on the Shift's work date.
- **R24.** After such a change a Timesheet the pool no longer covers loses its share unless it is locked, and a locked Timesheet the pool now covers gets none.
- **R25.** When [`REQ-TIME-0007`](#req-time-0007) locks a covered Timesheet while another, not a no-show, lacks a clock time, Iris sends TIP_HOURS_MISSING to the Unit Users R11 names, naming the pool and the Workers whose hours are missing.
- **R26.** TIP_HOURS_MISSING is sent at most once for a pool: sending it sets the pool's hours_missing_notified_at, and a pool that has it set sends none.

## Reporting

One spend definition, standard metrics, dashboards, and plain-language answers.

<a id="req-reporting-0001"></a>

### Define approved and pending spend once for every screen

`REQ-REPORTING-0001`

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Every screen, report, and answer uses one definition of spend, so the same question gives the same number everywhere. Spend is approved spend plus pending spend.
- **Why:**
  - Managers see spend only when the invoice lands, 2–4 weeks later *(REP-7: Operator spend dashboard: spend vs. budget, by supplier, vs. last month)*
  - Units want to know what last Friday's banquet actually cost, and some clients expect it the next morning *(REP-2: Event-level cost: group shifts into an event and see projected vs. actual, available the next morning)*
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §1 Detailed requirements; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-7; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-2; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §5 Invoices

**Rules**

- **R1.** SPEND is APPROVED_SPEND plus PENDING_SPEND, and every screen, report, and answer computes all three only as this requirement defines them.
- **R2.** APPROVED_SPEND is the sum, over Timesheets whose status is APPROVED, of regular, overtime, and double-time amounts at the Timesheet's Bill Rates, plus approved Expenses and allocated tips.
- **R4.** A Timesheet keeps counting toward APPROVED_SPEND after it locks.
- **R5.** An Expense counts at its amount, with no markup, only when the Expense and its Timesheet are both APPROVED, even if that Timesheet is a no-show.
- **R6.** A tip allocation counts at its amount, with no markup, once its Timesheet is APPROVED, and counts as zero while that Timesheet is a no-show.
- **R7.** PENDING_SPEND covers each Timesheet not yet APPROVED on a Shift whose end time has passed, at the hours entered, or at the scheduled hours when none are entered.
- **R8.** Entered hours are priced by hour class at the Timesheet's Bill Rates, and hours count as not entered when the clock-in or the clock-out is missing.
- **R9.** Scheduled hours are the Shift's end minus its start minus its planned break, priced at the Timesheet's regular Bill Rate.
- **R10.** PENDING_SPEND includes no tips and no Expenses.
- **R11.** A Timesheet marked as a no-show adds no hours amount and no tips to APPROVED_SPEND or PENDING_SPEND; an APPROVED Expense on it still counts under R5.
- **R12.** A CANCELLED Shift adds nothing to spend.
- **R13.** The work date of spend is the date its Shift starts, in the Unit's timezone.
- **R14.** Spend on a Timesheet is charged to its Department's cost center.
- **R15.** Spend rolls up from Unit to District, Region, and Sector along the org tree.
- **R16.** PENDING_SPEND has two parts, entered and estimated; the estimated part is what R9 prices from scheduled hours, and any answer can give the two parts apart.
- **R17.** Every percentage or rate a report shows is computed from unrounded totals and rounded half up to one decimal place, and an average Bill Rate half up to the cent.

<a id="req-reporting-0002"></a>

### Define the standard measures and the dimensions that group them

`REQ-REPORTING-0002`

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Hours, headcount, fill rate, and no-show rate each have one formula, and every measure groups by the same dimensions. The formulas are provisional: the sheet leaves metrics to be defined with Foodbuy.
- **Why:** No scorecards today; metrics to be defined with Foodbuy. MSP task: reports on SLAs and scorecards *(RC-16: Supplier scorecards and SLAs by agency: time to fill, fill rate, no-show rate, worker ratings, invoice accuracy)*
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §1 Metric definitions; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-16; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) 6.1

**Rules**

- **R1.** HOURS is the minutes behind SPEND, shown in hours: worked minutes on APPROVED Timesheets plus the entered or scheduled minutes counted in PENDING_SPEND.
- **R2.** OVERTIME_HOURS is the overtime and double-time minutes within HOURS, and scheduled minutes with no hours entered add none.
- **R3.** HEADCOUNT_REQUESTED is the sum of headcount on Shifts that are not CANCELLED.
- **R4.** FILL_RATE is ASSIGNED Assignments divided by headcount, over Shifts that have started.
- **R5.** Grouped by Agency, FILL_RATE divides the Agency's ASSIGNED Assignments by the headcount of the Releases sent to it, leaving out WITHDRAWN Releases.
- **R6.** NO_SHOW_RATE is Timesheets marked as a no-show divided by ASSIGNED Assignments, over Shifts whose status is WORKED.
- **R7.** A rate whose denominator is zero shows as not available, never as zero.
- **R8.** Every measure groups and filters by Sector, Region, District, Unit, Department, Company, Agency, Position, Event, work date, Work Week, and month.
- **R9.** For spend and hours, the Position and Department are the Timesheet's, which differ from the Shift's after a split, and the Agency is the Release's.
- **R10.** For HEADCOUNT_REQUESTED and FILL_RATE, the Position and Department are the Shift's, and for every measure the Event is the Shift's.
- **R11.** Grouping by Work Week puts each work date in the Work Week of its own Unit, and a month is a calendar month of work dates.

<a id="req-reporting-0003"></a>

### Answer plain-language questions with a chart, table, or dashboard

`REQ-REPORTING-0003`

- **Who:** Unit User, Program User
- **What:** A Unit User or a Program User asks a question about spend and labor in plain language and gets a chart, a table, or a dashboard. They can save the answer and reopen it.
- **Why:** Reporting today is Excel exports and a monthly PDF deck *(REP-1: Natural-language reporting: ask a question, get a chart, table or dashboard)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-1; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) 6.1; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Reporting

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User or a Program User asks a question in plain language, such as what was spent by Agency last week, and Iris answers with a chart or a table.
- **R2.** The LLM only turns the question into measures, groupings, filters, and a period, and code computes every number.
- **R3.** A question may use only the Measure enum's values: spend and its approved and pending parts, hours, overtime hours, headcount, fill rate, no-show rate, budget, labor percentage of sales, late Timesheets, and missed breaks.
- **R4.** An answer can be grouped or filtered by any dimension [`REQ-REPORTING-0002`](#req-reporting-0002) lists, down to one Event.
- **R5.** An answer with one measure grouped by one dimension is a bar chart, or a line chart when that dimension is work date, Work Week, or month; any other single-measure answer is a table.
- **R6.** An answer holds only records inside the asking User's scope, as [`REQ-ORG-0009`](#req-org-0009) checks: the Units under a Unit User's Role Grants, or the whole program for a Program User.
- **R7.** No measure uses a Pay Rate or a Markup, so no answer shows either one to any User.
- **R8.** When Iris cannot tell which measure or period a question means, it asks the User instead of guessing.
- **R9.** Asking a question saves nothing, so it needs no Proposal.
- **R10.** The User can save an answer under a name as a Saved Report, which stores the measures, groupings, filters, and period, not the numbers.
- **R11.** A Saved Report's period is either fixed start and end dates or one relative period, never both.
- **R12.** Only the User who saved a Saved Report can reopen it, and reopening recomputes it from current records within that User's current scope.
- **R13.** Only the User who saved a Saved Report can rename or delete it.
- **R14.** The relative periods are THIS_WORK_WEEK, LAST_WORK_WEEK, LAST_4_WORK_WEEKS, THIS_MONTH, and LAST_MONTH, each resolved when the report is opened, for each Unit in its own timezone and Work Week.
- **R15.** An answer with several measures is a dashboard that shows each measure as R5 would show it alone.

<a id="req-reporting-0004"></a>

### Show an Event's projected and actual cost the next morning

`REQ-REPORTING-0004`

- **Who:** Unit User, Program User
- **What:** For each Event, Iris shows the cost projected from its Releases beside the actual cost. Both are ready as soon as the Event's Shifts end, with any part still priced from scheduled hours shown as an estimate.
- **Why:** Units want to know what last Friday's banquet actually cost, and some clients expect it the next morning *(REP-2: Event-level cost: group shifts into an event and see projected vs. actual, available the next morning)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-2; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) 6.1

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Event's cost covers every Shift that names it as its Event.
- **R2.** Projected cost is the sum, over the Event's PENDING and ACCEPTED Releases, of headcount times scheduled minutes times the regular Bill Rate, divided by 60, rounded half up per Release.
- **R3.** Scheduled minutes are the Shift's end minus its start minus its planned break, and projected cost includes no tips and no Expenses.
- **R4.** Actual cost is the Event's SPEND under [`REQ-REPORTING-0001`](#req-reporting-0001), shown as APPROVED_SPEND and PENDING_SPEND, with the estimated part of PENDING_SPEND shown apart and labelled as an estimate.
- **R5.** Both costs are computed from current records when viewed, so a cost shows once the Event's last Shift ends; until hours are entered it is the estimate from scheduled hours, not what was worked.
- **R6.** Iris shows projected cost, actual cost, and the difference between them.
- **R7.** A Unit User sees Events at the Units in their scope, and a Program User sees every Event.

<a id="req-reporting-0005"></a>

### Upload sales data by Unit

`REQ-REPORTING-0005`

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User uploads sales by Unit and date: revenue, events held, and meals served. Iris stores them so labor cost can be shown as a percentage of sales.
- **Why:** Labor cost as a % of sales needs revenue data by location *(REP-4: Sales data upload by location)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-4; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Templates

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User uploads a SALES file, with one row per Unit and date.
- **R2.** Unit and date are required on every SALES row, and revenue, events, and meals served are each optional.
- **R3.** A SALES row is reported as a problem when its unit matches no Unit or more than one, its date is invalid, or its revenue, events, or meals served is not a number.
- **R4.** Two rows in one SALES file for the same Unit and date are reported as a problem.
- **R5.** A row for a Unit and date that already has a Sales Record is proposed as an update that replaces its revenue, events held, and meals served.
- **R6.** No SALES row is saved until the Program User approves the Proposal, and each accepted row is saved as a Sales Record linked to its Upload.

<a id="req-reporting-0006"></a>

### Show labor cost as a percentage of sales

`REQ-REPORTING-0006`

- **Who:** Unit User, Program User
- **What:** For a Unit or a group of Units and a period, Iris shows agency labor spend as a percentage of revenue. It uses only the dates that have revenue.
- **Why:** Managers should see total labor cost as % of sales, not a surprise invoice *(REP-3: Labor cost as a percentage of sales by location, using revenue data)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-3; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) 6.1

**Rules**

- **R1.** LABOR_PCT_OF_SALES is SPEND divided by revenue, times 100, over the Unit's work dates in the period that have revenue above zero.
- **R2.** A date with no Sales Record, or with empty or zero revenue, is left out of both the spend and the revenue.
- **R3.** For several Units, the measure divides their total included spend by their total included revenue.
- **R4.** When no date in the period has revenue, the measure shows as not available, never as zero.
- **R5.** Labor cost here is Spend under [`REQ-REPORTING-0001`](#req-reporting-0001), the agency labor held in Iris, and excludes Compass's own employees.
- **R6.** A Unit User sees the measure for the Units in their scope, and a Program User for any Unit.

<a id="req-reporting-0007"></a>

### Load Unit budgets from a file

`REQ-REPORTING-0007`

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User loads labor budgets from a file, one row per Unit and date range. Dashboards compare spend with the budget for any period.
- **Why:** Spend vs. budget needs budgets in Iris *(REP-8: Unit budgets loaded by bulk upload)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-8

**Rules**

- **R1.** Only a Program User uploads a BUDGETS file, and each row gives a Unit, a period start date, a period end date, and an amount, all required.
- **R2.** A Budget belongs to one Unit, and Department budgets are not part of MVP.
- **R3.** A BUDGETS row is reported as a problem when its unit matches no Unit or more than one, or its end date is before its start date.
- **R4.** A row whose dates overlap another Budget of the same Unit, saved or in the same file, is reported as a problem, unless its dates equal a saved Budget's.
- **R5.** A row with the same Unit and dates as a saved Budget is proposed as an update to its amount.
- **R6.** No BUDGETS row is saved until the Program User approves the Proposal, and each accepted row is saved as a Budget linked to its Upload.
- **R7.** BUDGET for a Unit and period is the sum of its Budgets' amounts, each prorated by the share of its days in the period and rounded half up to the cent before summing.
- **R8.** A period in which a Unit has no Budget day shows no budget rather than zero.

<a id="req-reporting-0008"></a>

### Show Unit Users spend against budget, by Agency, and against last month

`REQ-REPORTING-0008`

- **Who:** Unit User
- **What:** A Unit User sees spend for the Units in their scope against budget, by Agency, and against the prior week and month. A User granted above a Unit sees the same view rolled up.
- **Why:** Managers see spend only when the invoice lands, 2–4 weeks later *(REP-7: Operator spend dashboard: spend vs. budget, by supplier, vs. last month)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-7; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) 6.3; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §1 Detailed requirements

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Unit User sees the dashboard for every Unit inside the scope of their Role Grants and can narrow it to one Unit.
- **R2.** It shows SPEND for the current calendar month to date beside BUDGET for the whole month and the difference, and shows no budget where none is loaded.
- **R3.** It shows SPEND for the current month to date beside the whole prior month, and for the current Work Week to date beside the whole prior Work Week, each with its percentage change.
- **R4.** It splits every SPEND figure into APPROVED_SPEND and PENDING_SPEND.
- **R5.** It breaks the month's SPEND down by Agency, with each Agency's average Bill Rate: its spend on hours divided by its HOURS.
- **R6.** It breaks the month's SPEND down by Position and by Unit.
- **R7.** It shows the HOURS and HEADCOUNT_REQUESTED behind the month's SPEND.
- **R8.** A Unit User granted at a Sector, Region, or District sees the same dashboard rolled up across every Unit beneath that node.
- **R9.** Every number is computed from current records when the dashboard opens, so a Shift's cost appears as PENDING_SPEND as soon as the Shift ends.

<a id="req-reporting-0009"></a>

### Show Program Users top Agencies, Events, and Units with trends

`REQ-REPORTING-0009`

- **Who:** Program User
- **What:** A Program User sees which Agencies, Events, and Units carry the most spend, how spend moves over time, and how each Agency performs.
- **Why:** Program owners need trends and supplier performance *(REP-9: Program owner views: top suppliers, events and operators, with trends over time)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-9; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) 6.3

**Rules**

- **R1.** For a chosen period, a Program User sees Agencies, Events, and Units each ranked by SPEND, highest first.
- **R2.** A trend shows a measure per Work Week or per calendar month across the chosen period.
- **R3.** Each Agency shows its FILL_RATE and NO_SHOW_RATE beside its SPEND, as that Agency's performance.
- **R4.** Each Unit shows this month's SPEND as a percentage above or below the average of its prior full calendar months, up to three, with no flag threshold.
- **R5.** A Unit with no prior full calendar month of spend shows no comparison.
- **R6.** The views cover the whole program and can be filtered to a Sector, Region, or District.
- **R7.** Each Unit also shows how many of its Releases for work dates in the period carry a bill_rate_reason or have is_non_contracted set.

<a id="req-reporting-0010"></a>

### Report Timesheet compliance: missed breaks and late approvals

`REQ-REPORTING-0010`

- **Who:** Program User, Unit User
- **What:** Iris reports Timesheets with missed breaks and Timesheets approved late, for any period and grouping.
- **Why:** VMS requirement: timecard compliance reporting *(REP-10: Timecard compliance report: missed breaks and late approvals)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) REP-10; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) 6.3

**Rules**

- **R1.** For a chosen period, the report counts Timesheets with a missed break and late Timesheets, grouped by any dimension [`REQ-REPORTING-0002`](#req-reporting-0002) lists, such as Unit or Agency.
- **R2.** A Timesheet has a missed break when its exception reasons include MISSED_BREAK.
- **R3.** A Timesheet is late when it is not APPROVED by LOCK_WINDOW_HOURS after its Shift ends, and it stays counted as late if approved afterwards.
- **R4.** LOCK_WINDOW_HOURS is the value [`REQ-ORG-0006`](#req-org-0006) resolves for the Timesheet's Unit when the report is run, so a changed Setting changes which past Timesheets count as late.
- **R5.** LATE_TIMESHEETS counts late Timesheets by the work date of their Shift.
- **R6.** A Program User sees the report for the whole program, and a Unit User for the Units in their scope.
- **R7.** MISSED_BREAK_TIMESHEETS counts Timesheets with a missed break by the work date of their Shift.
